papers.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
papers.abstract:
$A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics.
  By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie.
  We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is unusual in that rather than defining them by localization, we construct our $\infty$-categories completely explicitly as simplicial sets.
  Our $\infty$-categories are intended for applications to Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry. Given a suitable symplectic manifold $(X,\omega)$, one should construct its Fukaya category ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a (filtered) $A_\infty$-category, and its derived Fukaya category $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a triangulated category (or better, a stable $\infty$-category). Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Our $\infty$-categories give a clean way to explain in what sense ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ and $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ are independent of these choices.

papers.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
papers.abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(\tau_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

papers.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
papers.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.

papers.title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology. Hence it is natural to ask whether the target also has height $m+n$. Although this fails in general, we prove that it holds whenever $R$ is connective and $m\geq1$. Our proof is based on an iterative calculation using Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology. As an application, we determine the support of the $T^n$-homotopy fixed points of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ for $n=2,3$ with $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ equipped with any $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-form.

papers.title: A simplicial model for manifold calculus through the configuration category
papers.abstract:
Let $M$ be a closed $d$-dimensional smooth manifold and $X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$ a finite simplicial set whose geometric realization is homeomorphic to $M$. Given the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ of disks embedded in $M$ and the path components functor $\pi_0:\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$, we construct a cofinal functor $\Gamma_X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ such that $X=\pi_0\circ\Gamma_X$.
  This result provides an alternative construction of a simplicial model developed by Boavida de Brito, Lambrechts, Pryor and Songhafouo Tsopm\'en\'e to compute the space-valued presheaf $\operatorname{Emb}(-,M):\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$. We also extend the result to manifolds with a $G$-structure and discuss applications to manifold calculus, factorization homology, and a possible generalization to manifolds with boundary.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity for polypositroids
papers.abstract: We prove that all coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of an integral polypositroid are strictly positive. In particular, this proves the positroid conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko and Schröter. More generally, inclusion of integral polypositroids in a common cyclic order implies coefficientwise comparison of their Ehrhart polynomials. Hence the hypersimplex dominates every positroid of the same rank and size. We express each coefficient as a sum of relative face volumes multiplied by explicit nonnegative rational weights. The weights count linear extensions and specialize, for hypersimplices, to Ferroni's formula involving weighted Lah and Eulerian numbers. In the appendix we exhibit two representable matroids whose quartic Ehrhart coefficients exceed those of the hypersimplices of the same rank and size.

papers.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
papers.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $\lambda$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $\Delta^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

papers.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

papers.title: A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism
papers.abstract: Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class. For the GM and $\mathrm{KT}^{\pm}$ cases, deleting tubular neighborhoods and identifying sphere-bundle structures with determinant-twisted base structures give a characteristic exact sequence. This proves the bordism-group consequence of the DYY conjecture for our definitions, without constructing the conjectured map of spectra.

papers.title: A stratified version of geometric realizations
papers.abstract: Given a simplicial set $X$, let $\operatorname{B}({X})$ denote its poset of nondegenerate simplices. We define a natural stratification $\left\vert{X}\right\vert\rightarrow\operatorname{B}({X})$. When $X$ is locally finite, we prove that this stratification is conical. Moreover, if $X$ is finite, we prove that the exit path category $\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ satisfies the geometric realization formula $\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\limits_{\sigma:\Delta[p]\rightarrow X} \operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({p})}(\Delta^p)\simeq\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ where the colimit is indexed by the category of simplices of $X$.

papers.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
papers.abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

papers.title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem
papers.abstract: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.

papers.title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.

papers.title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in \v{C}ech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates. We validate our approach through experiments on synthetic datasets, and present novel examples of $K(\mathbb{Z}/2, 2)$-coordinates not addressed in prior work.

papers.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
papers.abstract:
We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces.
  As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

papers.title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.

papers.title: Gersten exactness with invertible coefficients for excellent regular local surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an excellent regular local ring of dimension two, and let $N\geq2$ be a natural number invertible in $R$. We prove exactness of the augmented Gersten complex for $K(R;\mathbb{Z}/N)$ in every degree. More generally, it suffices that the normalization of every reduced closed curve in $\operatorname{Spec} R$ be finite. The proof applies to ramified mixed-characteristic rings without a henselianity assumption. With coefficients of invertible order, we first prove that pushforward from a Cartier divisor on the spectrum of a noetherian semilocal ring annihilates every class coming from connective $K$-theory. For a curve in $\operatorname{Spec} R$, we then place its normalization and auxiliary regular curves as transverse Cartier divisors on a finite $R$-scheme. A third curve carries a prescribed residue class, and a quotient of the two divisor equations moves that residue to an auxiliary curve. The residues on the auxiliary curves cancel after transfer to the residue field of $R$. These constructions prove generic injectivity; vanishing of the closed-point pushforward then gives the full complex.

papers.title: Graded version of local-global principle for Steinberg and Chevalley groups
papers.abstract: In this article, an analog of a graded version of Quillen-Suslin's local-global principle was established for Steinberg groups $St(\Phi,-)$ and Chevalley groups $G(\Phi,-)$ over a reduced irreducible root system $\Phi$.

papers.title: Unbounded traces, Connes' index theorem for measured foliations, and the Godbillon-Vey invariant in KK-theory
papers.abstract: We prove that unbounded positive traces define KK-elements with real coefficients. Such traces naturally arise from invariant transverse measures on foliations (Connes, 1979) and, more generally, on Lie groupoids (Crainic--Mestre, 2019). As an application, we build a canonical KK-element with real coefficients whose associated map of K-groups is the Godbillon-Vey invariant as constructed by Connes. In the process, we show how Connes' index theorem for measured foliations can be deduced from the Connes-Skandalis longitudinal index theorem, using cyclic cohomology.

papers.title: A Candidate Proof of the Fixed-Cartan Root Property for c-Vectors
papers.abstract: We present a candidate proof that every c-vector of a skew-symmetrizable cluster pattern with principal coefficients is a root of the Kac–Moody root system determined by the Cartan companion of the initial exchange matrix.

papers.title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
papers.abstract: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\ne\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(\Lambda)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.

papers.title: A Chebyshev bound for the constant in the Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: Let (A,B) be an ideal solution of size n of the Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem, with constant C defined by prod_i (x - a_i) - prod_i (x - b_i) = C, and let L be the diameter of A u B. We prove |C| <= 4 (L/4)^n, with equality exactly for the configuration given by the roots of T_n -/+ 1, where T_n is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Equality is attained by integer solutions for n <= 3 and, by Niven's theorem, is impossible for n >= 4; for n = 4, n = 5 and n = 6, however, we exhibit infinite families of integer solutions, governed by a Pell equation, along which the ratio 4^(n-1)|C|/L^n tends to 1, so that the constant 4^(n-1) cannot be improved. The bounds on C in the standard references are p-adic throughout: they determine which prime powers divide C, and the present inequality appears to be the first of archimedean type. Two further consequences are recorded: an unconditional lower bound for the height of any ideal solution, in terms of the known divisors of the universal constant C_n, which yields the first such statements for sizes 17 <= n <= 20, where no search has been published; and the observation that the extremal configuration is exactly the trigonometric configuration of Chen Shuwen, for which the analogous extremality statement for the individual variables is an open conjecture. The present result is its proven counterpart for the constant.

papers.title: A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent. Our proof follows the strategy of Kurano and Shimomoto and makes essential use of \v{C}esnavi\v{c}ius' Macaulayfication theorem.

papers.title: A counterexample to a stability question for unramified multiplicity one symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: We construct a split reductive symmetric pair over $\mathbb{Q}_{17}$ with multiplicity at most one for every irreducible unramified representation and which is not a stable symmetric pair.

papers.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $\lambda$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+\lambda=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\F_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\F_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.

papers.title: A four-state Markovian Mpemba effect in which every triplet test fails
papers.abstract: Avitan, Factor and Gelbwaser-Klimovsky derived necessary conditions on the transition rates of a three-level system for the Markovian Mpemba effect, and proposed applying them to every triplet of levels of an $N$-level system. For a zero-temperature bath and non-degenerate spectrum they proved that a strong violation of the conditions in all triplets excludes the effect; for non-zero temperature they conjectured, on the basis of numerical sampling, that violation in all triplets excludes it. We give an explicit reversible four-state chain, with energies $U(0,1,2,64)$ and a bath at inverse temperature $\ln 2/U$, in which all four triplet conditions fail strictly and yet a hotter thermal initial state has a strictly smaller slow-mode amplitude than a colder one. This is a direct Mpemba effect, so the finite-temperature conjecture fails for $N=4$. The example is marginal: it uses Boltzmann weights of order $2^{-64}$, initial temperatures of order $10^2\,U$, a relative amplitude gap of about $0.07\%$, and three of the four triplets fail by margins of order $10^{-6}$. We then give a second, less marginal example with energies $(0,\frac{1}{30},0.434,5)$, bath inverse temperature $3$ and initial inverse temperatures $0.06$ and $\frac{1}{6}$: every triplet fails by at least $1.08\times10^{-3}$ relative to its largest rate, and the relative amplitude gap is $1.22\%$. A variant of the second example with rational Boltzmann factors has the same properties and is certified in exact rational arithmetic without exponential enclosures. All claims are reduced to finite exact rational or rational-interval computations, which we describe. In both examples the ground level escapes more slowly than the slowest mode relaxes; an exact elimination identity shows that the slow mode then sees effective couplings between the excited levels that depend on the slowest eigenvalue, and these are not visible to tests built from the original rates.

papers.title: A Geometric Coding Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a direct analogue of the classical Coding Theorem in the setting of symmetry groups. We consider computable bijections on the set of binary strings and define the symmetry prior of a string x as the probability that a randomly chosen symmetry from a given group G has x as its unique fixed point. We show that for any fix-retractable symmetry group G, a group admitting a computable section that selects an isolating symmetry for every string, the symmetry prior is a universal lower semi-computable semi-measure. In this case, the Geometric Coding Theorem holds. This result is a coding-theoretic restatement of a theorem of Trejo, Kreinovich and Longpr\'e, who showed that the complexity of describing a string by a symmetry with that string as its unique fixed point equals its Kolmogorov complexity. Our contribution is to recast it in terms of algorithmic probability and to treat the symmetry group as a parameter, identifying fix-retractability as exactly the condition under which symmetry complexity collapses onto Kolmogorov complexity.

papers.title: A height criterion for irrational weight-three Lambert sums
papers.abstract: For an algebraic number $b$ with $|b|>1$, the weight-three Lambert sum is $Z(b)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^2/(b^n-1)$. We prove that $Z(b)$ lies outside $\mathbb{Q}(b)$ whenever the Mahler measure $M(b)$ satisfies $\log M(b)<(352\pi^2/2889)\,r\log|b|$, where $r=1$ for a real base and $r=2$ otherwise. The criterion allows several conjugates outside the unit disk and applies to nonintegral bases. In particular, $Z(3+\sqrt{3})\notin\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{3})$, although both conjugates of the base exceed one.

papers.title: A note on tropical convexity
papers.abstract: We prove that the tropicalization of the regular function $h=(x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2)/(x_1x_2x_3)$ on the coefficient-free Markov cluster threefold is not min-convex. This disproves Conjecture 8.11 of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.

papers.title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.

papers.title: A step to compute the determinant of finite semigroups not in ECom
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to begin studying the computation of the nonzero determinant of semigroups within the class of finite semigroups that possesses a pair of non-commutative idempotents. This paper focuses on a class of these semigroups introduced as $\ll$-smooth semigroups. This computation is applicable in the context of the extension of the MacWilliams theorem for codes over semigroup algebras.

papers.title: A weighted reciprocal Lucas sum lies outside ℚ(√5)
papers.abstract: For the even-indexed Lucas numbers $L_{2n}$, the reciprocal sums with numerators $1$ and $n^2$ are known to be transcendental. We prove that the intermediate sum $\sum_{n\ge1}n/L_{2n}$ lies outside $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and that the same conclusion holds with $L_{2an}$ in the denominator for every integer $a\ge1$. More generally, the weight-two value $\beta_{1/b}(2)=\sum_{n\ge1}n/(b^n+b^{-n})$ of the $q$-analogue of Dirichlet's beta function lies outside $\mathbb{Q}(b)$ for every real algebraic integer $b>1$ whose other conjugates have modulus at most one.

papers.title: Affine Supertrusses and Superbraces
papers.abstract: Brzezi\'nski's trusses are ''ring-like'' algebraic structures in which the addition is replaced with an abelian heap operation and the binary product satisfies a natural distributivity rule over the ternary addition. This paper addresses the question of how to define affine super-versions of trusses. Taking our cue from the theory of algebraic supergroups, we define an affine supertruss as a representable functor from the category of unital associative supercommutative superalgebras to the category of trusses. The representing superalgebras are equipped with a ''cotruss'' structure-a new concept in itself. We show that from an affine supertruss, provided the binary product defines a supergroup, one can construct an affine two-sided superbrace, and so generalise Rump's braces to supermathematics. As an application of these constructions, we propose a generalisation of the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation to the setting of affine superschemes via a super-version of Adler's map.

papers.title: An asymptotic lower bound for the number of irrational even beta values
papers.abstract: For even $s$, let $I(s)$ count the irrational values among $\beta(2),\beta(4),\ldots,\beta(s)$. We prove $\liminf_{\substack{s\to\infty\\2\mid s}} \frac{I(s)}{\sqrt{s\log\log s/\log s}} \geq 2\sqrt{\frac{\zeta(2)\zeta(3)}{3\zeta(6)}} \approx 1.6098018250$. Here $\beta$ denotes the Dirichlet beta function and $\zeta$ the Riemann zeta function. The bound improves the growth rate in our earlier counting result by a factor $\sqrt{\log\log s}$. It has the same growth rate as the recent theorem of Fischler, Lai, Sprang and Zudilin for irrational odd zeta values, with $1/\sqrt3$ of their leading constant. The conclusion remains valid after any fixed initial set of even beta values is omitted.

papers.title: An explicit formal dual for every configuration $\Gamma(C,C^\perp)$ of Bierbrauer–Edel's definition, and formal isoduality of the packings in dimensions 18, 28 and 30
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a binary linear $[2k,k]$ code with $C\neq C^\perp$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(C,C^\perp)$ the configuration of formula (1), the definition on p. 97 of Bierbrauer–Edel. Theorem A gives an explicit formal dual of $\Gamma$ in the sense of Cohn–Kumar–Reiher–Schürmann, in terms of $C$, $C^\perp$ and two auxiliary words. No hypothesis on minimum distance or parity is needed. The finite pair behind it has $|S|=|T|=2^{r+1}$ in a group of order $2^{2r+2}$, where $r=k-\dim R$ and $R=C\cap C^\perp$ is the hull of $C$. Proposition I shows that this dual is an isometric copy of $\Gamma/8$. So $\Gamma$ rescaled to unit density is formally isodual in the sense of Cohn–Kumar–Schürmann. A remark shows that it is formally self-dual exactly when $4\mid n$ and the hull is doubly even. Hence the packings 18.1, 28.1 and 30.1 are formally isodual and not formally self-dual. A further remark concerns codes with $\mathbf 1\in R$ and $r=4,6,8$: an $\mathbb F_2$-linear identification turns $S$ into a graph $\{(x,F(x)) : x\in\mathbb F_{2^{r+1}}\}$ with $F$ a permutation, formally self-dual under the trace pairing of Kölsch–Schüler. The same construction was also run for $r=10,12$: computed, not reviewed.

papers.title: An Extremal Vertex Operator Algebra of Central Charge c=64
papers.abstract: Starting with the standard self-dual \((-1)\)-orbifold of the Barnes--Wall lattice VOA of central charge \(32\), we construct a simple-current extension of a fixed-point subalgebra of its tensor square. The resulting vertex operator algebra is self-dual of central charge \(64\) and has no nonzero Virasoro highest-weight vector of weight \(1\) or \(2\). We give the twisted conformal weights, an elementary proof of the group-cohomological detection statement needed to trivialize the twisted-module associator class, and a permutation-cover argument determining the relevant absolute module weights. This identifies the complete weight-two obstruction set in a \(56\)-dimensional binary quadratic space. An explicit \(28\)-dimensional totally singular graph avoids that set; its exhaustive verifier is included. The final algebra object and its multiplication are also explicit. To my knowledge, this is the first new central-charge value of an extremal self-dual vertex operator algebra since the examples discussed in my 1995 thesis.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for proper connective DG-algebras via extended module categories
papers.abstract: We establish a $d$-dimensional Auslander correspondence for $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebras via $d$-extended module categories. A $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $\Gamma$ is called Auslander if its $d$-extended module category is a $d$-Auslander extriangulated category. Our main theorem gives a one-to-one correspondence: for any $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $\Lambda$ whose $d$-extended module category has finitely many indecomposable objects, the endomorphism DG-algebra of an additive generator is Auslander, and conversely every Auslander $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra arises in this way.

papers.title: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
papers.abstract: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: BKT asymptotics for the quenched free energy of hierarchical pinning
papers.abstract: We study the disordered pinning model of Derrida, Hakim and Vannimenus on the diamond hierarchical lattice. Its partition functions satisfy $R_{n+1}\overset{d}{=}(R_n^{(1)}R_n^{(2)}+B-1)/B$, where $B>2$, the two variables on the right are independent copies of $R_n$, and $R_0=e^hW$ with $W>0$ and $\mathbb{E}W=1$. Let $F$ be the quenched free energy and $h_c$ its critical point. If $h_c>\log(B-1)$, we prove $F(h_c+u)=\exp[-(K+o(1))/\sqrt{u}]$ as $u\downarrow0$, for a finite positive constant $K$ characterized by the response at criticality to a change of field. We identify a limiting profile of the rescaled tilted measures and extend their convergence in exponential weights to every time before its first pole. This yields the free-energy upper bound; a comparison with a max-type recursion and a second-moment estimate for pairs of leaves give the matching lower bound. A Lean 4 formalization of the main results accompanies the paper.

papers.title: Black-box identity testing for affine orbits of read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs
papers.abstract: For every fixed width, we construct a polynomial-size hitting set for read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs under an unknown invertible affine change of variables. A width bound in a single unknown order suffices. The resulting deterministic black-box identity test runs in time polynomial in the number of variables and the total degree over every field with more elements than the degree. The construction preserves the generic ranks of consecutive matrix products in descending order. At fixed dimension and width, the query count is linear in the total degree in characteristic zero or above the individual degree in the hidden coordinates. When the width bound holds in every order, cut ranks give linear dependence up to logarithmic factors even in small characteristic. We also treat multivariate layers with bounded overlap and obtain a linear query bound for bivariate programs of width two.

papers.title: Can moving the mouths of a self-supporting wormhole make a shortcut? A no-shortcut theorem in a two-dimensional loop model
papers.abstract: The Morris-Thorne-Yurtsever route to a time machine moves one wormhole mouth so that a twin-paradox lag becomes a time shift between the mouths. For wormholes supported by their own Casimir-like energy (Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov) the static throat is longer than the exterior path; we know of no explicit dynamical calculation for moving mouths. We study a toy model in which the question can be posed exactly: a JT-gravity throat whose two boundaries are transparent to conformal matter that also propagates through a rigid flat exterior. We prove that in this model no timelike motion of the mouths produces a shortcut through the throat in either direction, as long as both mouth clocks keep running. The proof combines (i) a lap identity, by which there is no shortcut iff a Dirichlet operator built from one mouth's Schwarzian energy is non-negative on each lap of a matter stream; (ii) a sum rule equating the averaged null energy along each complete null geodesic of the throat to $-\beta/2$ times the sum of the clock rates at its ends, which is the dynamical form of a relation of Maldacena and Qi and is not claimed as new; and (iii) a variational step. With the quantum inequality for the streams the same steps exclude a shortcut for any agent acting locally on the streams in the exterior. Two partial lower bounds on the size of the margin are given; no positive floor is proven. Simulations from one code base illustrate the results. The model has a non-gravitating exterior and a classical Schwarzian mode, and nothing is claimed about four dimensions. The derivations, code and text were produced with AI assistance under the author's direction; Section 6 states what was checked and by whom. No physicist has checked this work.

papers.title: Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras
papers.abstract: This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem for their simple quotients under certain conditions. If $A$ is finite-dimensional, we prove that its orthogonal idempotent decomposition into local Artinian summands naturally induces a tensor product isomorphism of the corresponding vertex operator superalgebras. In addition, our general construction encompasses many vertex operator superalgebras, such as superconformal algebras and generalized $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ (super)algebras.

papers.title: Christol’s Conjecture for Non-Resonant Globally Bounded ₃F₂(a₁, a₂, a₃; b, 1; x) Series
papers.abstract: Christol conjectured that every globally bounded, D-finite power series with rational coefficients is the diagonal of a rational function. We prove this for the hypergeometric series ${}_3F_2(a_1,a_2,a_3;b,1;x)$ with rational parameters such that $a_i$, $b$ and $a_i-b$ are not integers: if such a series is globally bounded, then it is the diagonal of an algebraic power series in two variables, and hence of a rational function in three variables; three is the least possible number of variables. This includes Christol's example ${}_3F_2(\frac19,\frac49,\frac59;\frac13,1;x)$ from 1987, and the series ${}_3F_2(\frac17,\frac27,\frac47;\frac12,1;x)$, which Christol suggested as a possible counterexample to his conjecture. By a result of Rivoal and Roques, under the Rohrlich-Lang conjecture the latter is a diagonal that is not a Hadamard product of algebraic power series. The proof is Hodge-theoretic and not constructive: it shows that such diagonal representations exist, but does not produce them. Using Fedorov's formula for the Hodge numbers of hypergeometric local systems, we show that the series is globally bounded exactly when every Galois conjugate of its local system carries a complex variation of Hodge structure with two adjacent Hodge levels. The restriction of scalars of the local system then underlies a polarized integral variation of Hodge structure of weight one. By a theorem of Deligne the series is therefore a period of an abelian scheme, and hence of a family of curves, where it is an integral over vanishing cycles of a semistable degeneration. Expanding this integral at the nodes of a regular model gives the diagonal representation.

papers.title: Circle configurations and the hardness of promise graph and hypergraph coloring
papers.abstract: In 2017 Brakensiek and Guruswami conjectured that promise graph homomorphism is NP-hard for every non-bipartite source and loopless target admitting a homomorphism from the source. At CCC 2016 they conjectured hardness of properly coloring a uniform hypergraph promised a strong coloring with one more color than its uniformity. We prove both conjectures by a configuration theorem on the circle. For any fixed finite configuration of distinct rational phases, the theorem gives a reduction whose satisfiable instances place every edge near a translate of the configuration and whose unsatisfiable instances have arbitrarily small independence ratio. An antipodal pair gives hardness for every odd cycle against every fixed clique of size at least three. A regular $h$-gon gives a strong $(h+1)$-coloring and a rainbow $(h-1)$-coloring of the same instance. A circle coloring built from single-coordinate changes gives hardness of $\mathrm{PCSP}(R,\mathrm{NAE}_h^{(d)})$ for every nonempty symmetric reconfigurable relation $R$ with $R\to\mathrm{NAE}_h^{(d)}$, and the monochromatic-clique dichotomy of Banakh, Barsukov, and Nakajima without the Rich $2$-to-$1$ Conjecture. For triples we obtain hardness of linearly ordered coloring for all fixed palettes $3\le c\le d$. The proof subtracts an average of translated distance functions to detect an independent set, then uses conditional mean zero and a finite Ramsey alignment argument to decode a Label Cover assignment.

papers.title: Cohomology Rings of Fiber Products of Lefschetz Fibrations
papers.abstract: We prove a Lefschetz-type theorem for the cohomology rings of fiber products of two Lefschetz fibrations with disjoint critical loci. As an application, we compute the Hodge numbers of several examples of higher-dimensional Schoen's Calabi-Yau manifolds.

papers.title: Coinvariants of metaplectic representations on moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We construct spaces of coinvariants at principally polarized abelian varieties with respect to the action of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra. We show how these spaces globalize to twisted $\mathscr{D}$-modules on moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties, and we determine the Atiyah algebra of a line bundle acting on them. We prove analogous results on the universal abelian variety. An essential aspect of our study involves analyzing the Atiyah algebra of the Hodge and canonical line bundles on moduli of abelian varieties and the universal abelian variety.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions.

papers.title: Complete modulus locking in the exceptional set of the abc conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $N_\lambda(X)$ count primitive positive triples $a+b=c\le X$ with $\mathrm{rad}(abc)<c^\lambda$. We prove, using inherited anatomic estimates and a new finite exact-rational implication, that $N_\lambda(X)\ll_{\lambda,\varepsilon}X^{U+\varepsilon}$ for $0<\lambda\le1$, where $U=\frac{11680007}{20000012}<\frac{73}{125}=0.584$. The new arithmetic-computational step exhausts all third-letter whole-value modulus sets: index $1$ is eliminated by a one-Lipschitz argument, leaving $32$ subsets of $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, and grouped power-difference bounds are used in every fixed degree $2\le e\le6$. A branch-and-bound tree with $65{,}576$ leaves is verified by an independent standard-library checker which reconstructs every inequality and checks every rational multiplier; floating-point linear programming is used only to discover the tree. We also prove that the enlargement is mathematically essential: an explicit rational point feasible for the old modulus family has $D=403/690$, whereas FullOC gives the collision bound $53/92$ at the same point, and a second explicit point gives $7/12\le D^*_{\mathrm{FullOC}}$. These are statements about exponent programs, not lower bounds for abc triples. No assertion of abc, Szpiro, finiteness of the exceptional set, or an Arakelov degeneration functor is made.

papers.title: Complete positivity and equilibrium realizations of reversible observations
papers.abstract: Complete positivity of mirrored observation matrices is necessary for equilibrium realization, but does not ensure compatible equilibrium dynamics. We study stationary finite-state continuous-time Markov chains with instantaneous deterministic labels on a fixed physical clock. For reflection-positive laws with $d$ active labels and reflected rank $r\le d+1$, we construct a detailed-balance realization on the minimal number $r$ of states. Binary rank-four laws with two prediction dimensions per label compress to four states when a finite detailed-balance realization already exists. At $r=d+2$, a rational ten-state chain with six labels passes every mirrored matrix-CP test through one common nonnegative Gram factorization, yet admits no equilibrium realization. A rational seven-time statistic separates its law from all finite equilibrium observation laws, uniformly over hidden dimensions, rates and topology. It gives a positive entropy-production floor for every exact finite reciprocal realization, with conservative constants too small for practical statistical use. The law also has no ordinary symmetric Markov extension on any standard Borel state space at the original clock, despite factorability of its reflected half-path operator. For laws that fail a matrix-CP test, a separate deletion-deficit theorem gives a computable nonlinear dissipation bound.

papers.title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
papers.abstract: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent. We also show that the equivariant central charges have no poles in the spectral parameter, compute their monodromy and their asymptotics at $z=0$, and formulate an equivariant mirror symmetry conjecture for GKM manifolds.

papers.title: Counterexamples to coefficient conjectures for plane Penrose polynomials
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to coefficient-sign alternation and coefficient nonvanishing for the plane Penrose polynomial $P_H(q)=\sum_{A\subseteq E(H)}(-1)^{|A|}q^{c_H(A)}$. Here $H$ is a graph embedded in the sphere, and $c_H(A)$ counts boundary components after replacing vertices by disks and edges by bands and half-twisting the bands in $A$. Weak alternation means that coefficients, read in descending powers from a positive leading coefficient, are alternately nonnegative and nonpositive. We construct a simple bridgeless plane graph on ten vertices whose Penrose polynomial is monic of degree eight and has linear coefficient $160$, contrary to weak alternation. A bridgeless plane multigraph on eleven vertices has zero linear coefficient. We also give a simple bridgeless cubic example on twelve vertices, where cubic means that every vertex has degree three; its linear and quadratic coefficients both have the wrong signs. These examples answer Aigner's questions on coefficient nonvanishing and sign alternation negatively. Replacing each degree-$k$ vertex of the first two examples by a $k$-cycle, with the incident edges attached in their embedding order, gives counterexamples to both coefficient conjectures of Kauffman, Silver and Williams. A known triangle-replacement identity gives infinite families, and connected sums give arbitrarily many vanishing initial coefficients for the Penrose–Kauffman polynomial. The cycle matroid of the ten-vertex example is an explicit planar minor-minimal obstruction to coefficient alternation, answering Aigner's question about minor-minimal binary-matroid obstructions negatively.

papers.title: Counting powerful products of consecutive integers
papers.abstract: We show that the number of $n\le x$ for which $n$ and $n+1$ are both powerful is $O_\varepsilon(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$, improving the exponent $29/100$ of Reuss. For each fixed $k\ge 3$ we show that the number of $n\le x$ for which $(n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+k)$ is powerful is $O_{k,\varepsilon}(x^{77/320+\varepsilon})$, and we prove the same exponent uniformly over all widths $k\ge3$. The new ingredient is a per-interval count in Reuss's form of Heath-Brown's approximate determinant method: in lattice-reduced coordinates, the solutions on an auxiliary curve of bidegree $(\alpha,\beta)$ become integral points of height at most $L_1^3T_1^2$ on an affine curve of degree $2\alpha+3\beta$, to which the uniform bound of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen applies. The proofs are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib and checked by Lean's kernel and an independent kernel; the formal statements take six theorems from the literature as explicit hypotheses. The results and exposition were produced and reviewed using AI systems; no human mathematical review has been performed. Section 10 describes the verification and its scope.

papers.title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
papers.abstract: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $\chi=\chi(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2\chi+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2\chi+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.

papers.title: Daboussi's elementary proof of the prime number theorem, reconsidered
papers.abstract: In 1984, Daboussi gave an "elementary" proof of the prime number theorem whose central actors are smooth numbers (numbers with no large prime factors). We explain a variant of his argument that might be considered even more elementary.

papers.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
papers.abstract: We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Mont\'ufar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.

papers.title: Deterministic almost-linear time for general matching and network flow
papers.abstract: We give deterministic almost-linear-time algorithms for maximum-cardinality matching in general graphs and integral minimum-cost flow. With $H = n + m + 2$, both run in $H \exp O((\log H)^{4/5}(\log \log H)^{1/5})$ time for polynomially bounded integer flow data. Their circulation oracle charges every traversal of a returned walk. A clipped logarithmic potential handles flow thresholds under improving updates and maintains strong components under arc insertions. For subgraphs with degree bounds, two matching computations encode a factor of every feasible size. The underlying exchange argument also gives integral cardinality slices for capacitated factors and is compatible with sharp local rounding.

papers.title: Duality for Cohen--Macaulay Complexes through Combinatorial Sheaves
papers.abstract: We prove a duality theorem for Cohen--Macaulay simplicial complexes. This is a generalisation of Poincar\'e Duality, framed in the language of combinatorial sheaves. Our treatment is self-contained and accessible for readers with a working knowledge of simplicial complexes and (co)homology. The main motivation is a link with Bieri-Eckmann duality for discrete groups, which is explored in a companion paper.

papers.title: Dyson's Tenfold Way, Revisited
papers.abstract:
In this work, we study semilinear representations of groups acting on degree two Galois extensions. Our results include a classification of irreducible semilinear representations, which generalises Dyson's Tenfold Way. Using this, we completely describe the semilinear representation theory of certain groups, such as symmetric groups, and of finite groups over cyclotomic fields.
  We also prove many results concerning semilinear representations over $\mathbb{C}$, which includes an induction theorem which simultaneously generalises Brauer's Induction Theorem and Serre's Induction Theorem. We are also interested in applications of our classification theorem to crystallography, and include a detailed study of the semilinear representation theory of magnetic wallpaper groups.

papers.title: Entropy Production under Hidden-State Reduction: Exact Safety and Non-Testability
papers.abstract: Restricting hidden-state complexity can raise the least entropy production compatible with partial observations. We determine exactly when a two-hidden-state fit preserves this lower bound for finite irreducible stationary reciprocal continuous-time Markov chains with two individually observed states and one hidden label. We begin with an explicit chain with three hidden states whose observed data admit exact two-hidden-state fits, every one of which has entropy production more than sixty times that of the true chain. For strictly positive consistent stationary masses, flows, excursion counts and first duration moments, the unrestricted infimum is an explicit count functional, and four hidden states approach it while preserving every datum exactly. We classify finite attainment and safety of feasible two-hidden-state fits in every determinant regime; in the positive-determinant regime, safety is equivalent to equality of the conditional cross-excursion means, and explicit bounds quantify the reduction bias. Exact classification does not imply finite-data detectability: rare long excursions can conceal a fixed positive bias on any prescribed finite interval of stationary label observation, even under a common upper rate bound.

papers.title: Equal prime divisors in disjoint blocks of consecutive integers
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many disjoint pairs of consecutive blocks, of lengths three and four in that order, whose products have identical prime divisors. Their starting positions disprove the finiteness and separation predictions in Erdős’s 1976 formulation. The modern Erdős problem 931 requires the earlier block to be at least as long as the later one and remains open. For any fixed lengths \(k,\ell\ge2\), the number of equal-support pairs with increasing first terms at most \(X\), even allowing overlap, is \(O_{k,\ell,\varepsilon}(X^{2/3+\varepsilon})\). In the modern length order, we prove finiteness on fixed conics, on fixed equations in separated rational functions, and for pairs admitting two independent multiplicative relations. We also give exact counts in three strips of bounded separation, without a bound on either starting term.

papers.title: Euclidean interval objects in categories with finite products
papers.abstract: Based on the intuitive notion of convexity, we formulate a universal property defining interval objects in a category with finite products. Interval objects are structures corresponding to closed intervals of the real line, but their definition does not assume a pre-existing notion of real number. The universal property characterises such structures up to isomorphism, supports the definition of functions between intervals, and provides a means of verifying identities between functions. In the category of sets, the universal property characterises closed intervals of real numbers with nonempty interior. In the category of topological spaces, we obtain intervals with the Euclidean topology. We also prove that every elementary topos with natural numbers object contains an interval object; furthermore, we characterise interval objects as intervals of real numbers in the Cauchy completion of the rational numbers within the Dedekind reals.

papers.title: Exact minimum-cost arborescences under a single arc failure
papers.abstract: Every rooted weighted digraph on n vertices has a subgraph with $O(n^{3/2})$ arcs that contains a minimum-cost spanning arborescence after any feasible single arc deletion, answering a question of Dey and Kavitha. An oracle of the same size reports an optimal arborescence or a shortest list of arc replacements in time linear in the output. The construction uses shortest cycles in a weighted matroid exchange graph and admits deterministic subcubic preprocessing on simple digraphs. A reduction from directed distance preservation gives an $\Omega(n^{4/3} \log n)$-bit lower bound for reporting on simple digraphs with input arc identifiers, even with constant per-query error.

papers.title: Exact Sumsets of Primitive Quadratic Norms
papers.abstract: We determine the exact binary sumsets of primitive quadratic norm values at discriminants \(-3,-7,-8,-11\). The local congruence conditions are sufficient in three cases; at discriminant \(-7\) the complete additional exception set is \(\{7,77,203\}\). Stronger split-prime core identities separate the ramified dilations. The proofs combine quaternionic norm shells, precisely normalized classical Hecke bounds, and dyadic and ramified local filters. Explicit infinite estimates, rational interval certificates, complete finite sumset scans and multiplicative descent cover every positive target. We supply standalone verification code and explain the finite reductions that make the certificates complete. All sumsets concern numerical values, without coordinate multiplicities.

papers.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
papers.abstract: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to compute the coefficients. To illustrate the method, we compute the terms for the Virasoro extremal projector up to order 6. Furthermore, we formulate a conjecture for the denominators of the truncated extremal projector of the Virasoro algebra. We provide symbolic computational evidence up to order 6 and prove a weaker version of the conjecture.

papers.title: Finite model spaces and coherent sheaf models
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a finitary coherent theory with finitely many sorts. We describe coherent sheaf-valued models over a Stone space as continuous families in a topological category of finite $T$-models and all their homomorphisms. We prove that every such family over every Stone base is constant up to isomorphism on a finite clopen partition if and only if each fixed finite carrier admits only finitely many $T$-structures. It suffices to test the partition property over $\beta\mathbb N$. Equivalently, at each bound on the sort cardinalities, a finite subsignature detects all homomorphisms between the bounded models. This condition holds for finite signatures and is invariant under coherent Morita equivalence. It characterizes when the canonical functor from the discrete condensed category of finite models to the coherent condensed category of points is an equivalence. For finite locally constant abelian-group sheaves, we compute first Yoneda extensions as sections of a finite locally constant sheaf and prove that all higher Yoneda extensions in their category vanish.

papers.title: Finite-resolution information about a common clock: alias depth, holding-time loss, and the sampled Ehrenfest chain
papers.abstract: We study how much Fisher information about a common rate multiplier survives when a reaction system is observed only at discrete times. For a finite known mark law, the first loss at short sampling times is governed by an alias depth $h$, the smallest length mismatch among reaction-count fibres: the unrecovered fraction of reaction-count information is $1-F_p(\lambda)=C_p\lambda^{h-1}+O(\lambda^h)$ with an explicit alias coefficient $C_p$. For a fixed irreducible finite generator, holding times add a separate loss: the missing log-clock information is $A_2t^2+O(t^3)$, or $(A_3+H)t^3+O(t^4)$ when $A_2=0$. As a worked example we treat the stationary symmetric Ehrenfest chain of known size $\Omega$ observed at its endpoints, with sampling time $t$ and $\lambda=\Omega t$. For every population and every finite positive $t$, the exact endpoint information lies between an explicit quadratic lower bound and its matched Gaussian benchmark, $B_n\le R_n<g(t)/\lambda$, with relative width at most $1/(2\lambda)$ measured from $B_n$. The symmetric compound-Poisson benchmark is uniformly relatively accurate on $1\le\lambda\le L_\Omega$ if and only if $L_\Omega=o(\Omega)$. A formula-level comparison with the binomial AR(1) literature (Cui–Lund; Weiß–Kim) has not been completed.

papers.title: Flip-connectivity of octonion bracketing classes
papers.abstract: Substitute octonions for the letters of a word $w$. Each bracketing of $w$ is a polynomial map, and bracketings giving the same map form a kernel class inside the associahedron $K_n$ (edges: flips $(AB)C \leftrightarrow A(BC)$). Theorem. Every kernel class is flip-connected iff $w$ has at most two distinct letters or every letter occupies one contiguous run. Hence for $n \ge 1$, exactly $\mathrm{Bell}(n) - 2^n + n$ words of length $n$, up to renaming, have a disconnected class ($0,0,0,3,25,145,756,\dots$). Ideas. In-class flips must have letter-count matrix of rank $\le 2$: for any nonzero $3\times 3$ minor $d$ and $M = 2|d|+1$, an integer witness gives $[A,B,C] \equiv 2dM^3 e_7 \pmod{M^4}$. For interval words, the rank-$\le 2$ components are separated by octonion moments that recover an explicit component invariant. For other words, “caterpillar” certificates give two Moufang-equivalent bracketings that no rank-$\le 2$ path joins. Formalization. The main theorem, the canonical-word correspondence and the count are proved in core Lean 4 (no Mathlib): MainThm.main, Canon.canonical, Count.count_disconnected. That is 9,252 lines in lean/Caterpillar/, no sorry, standard axioms only. The one informal step is that polynomial identities over $\mathbb{Z}^8$ and over $\mathbb{R}^8$ agree. Disclosure. The formal proofs and much of the exposition were developed with Claude (Anthropic) under my direction. An AI referee round was done before posting (paper/REVIEW.md). I’m posting for independent human judgement, especially on Proposition T, which the paper proves via the formalization. I’d also like to know whether the associative-spectrum corollary $s_n(G) = C_{n-1}$ (Catalan numbers) is already in the literature. The paper’s two-line proof gives it for every non-associative magma with a two-sided identity, in particular for $\mathbb{O}$. Repository: https://github.com/Dojo-1/Lemma-W-count-determinant-witness-

papers.title: Fourier Epicycles and Antisymmetric Signed-Area Conservation in Normalized Riemann Zeta Terms
papers.abstract: In companion studies of Euler's alternating series $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ and its prime-base normalizations $\eta_p(s) = (1 - p^{1-s})\zeta(s)$, distributing the prefactor $(1 - p^{1-s})^{-1}$ across individual summands $t_{p,n}(s) = c_p(n)(1 - p^{1-s})^{-1}n^{-s}$ exposed an infinite hierarchy of closed, irreducible degree-$2k$ plane algebraic curves $t_{p,p^k}(\frac{1}{2}+ib)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[x, y]$ on the critical line $\operatorname{Re}(s) = \frac{1}{2}$, whose enclosed signed areas satisfy $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{signed}}(t_4) = 0$ at the base-$2$ Bernoulli lemniscate and $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{signed}}(t_{p,p^k}) = 0$ across every prime tower. Rather than keeping $(1 - p^{1-s})^{-1}$ unexpanded to preserve Cartesian curve equations, this paper expands $(1 - p^{1-s})^{-1} = -\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} p^{m(s-1)}$ across the critical strip $0 < \operatorname{Re}(s) < 1$ and distributes it termwise as a Fourier epicycle series. For every pure power $n = p^k$ ($k \ge 1$) along $s = a + ib$, the distributed expansion separates into $k - 1$ clockwise circles ($1 \le m \le k - 1$), a motionless center-of-mass anchor $+(p - 1)p^{-k}$ ($m = k$) independent of $s$, and an infinite counterclockwise tail ($m \ge k + 1$), revealing index-by-index how counter-rotating harmonics fold and area-balance the Lemniscate of Bernoulli $t_4(\frac{1}{2}+ib)$. Evaluating Green's theorem via Parseval's identity yields an exact closed-form signed-area formula for $t_{p,p^k}(a+ib)$ across $0 < a < 1$, proving that $t_4(a+ib)$ encloses zero net signed area if and only if $a = \frac{1}{2}$---tipping toward its clockwise left lobe for $0 < a < \frac{1}{2}$ and its counterclockwise right lobe for $\frac{1}{2} < a < 1$. Summing over $k \ge 1$ further proves that the total pure-power signed area $\mathcal{S}_p(a)$ is strictly antisymmetric across the critical line ($\mathcal{S}_p(1 - a) = -\mathcal{S}_p(a)$), negative on $0 < a < \frac{1}{2}$, positive on $\frac{1}{2} < a < 1$, and zero if and only if $\operatorname{Re}(s) = \frac{1}{2}$.

papers.title: From Multirelations to Meet-Relations: A Relational Duality for Semilattices with Adjunctions
papers.abstract: We develop a relational duality for semilattices with adjunctions (SLatas) based on binary meet-relations. First, we introduce the category of MoS-spaces and establish a dual equivalence with modal semilattices. Then, by means of A-relations, we define the category RelSP and prove a dual equivalence between SLata and RelSP. To compare this framework with the multirelational semantics previously developed for SLatas, we introduce the notion of normal mS-space and show that, under this condition, the multirelational structure can be canonically recovered from a meet-relation, and conversely. As a consequence, we prove that the categories RelSP and SLataSp are isomorphic.

papers.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
papers.abstract: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of natural transformations $\mathrm{id}\to F$ to the orthogonal complement of the collection, and it is computed from the collection by a finite complex. For collections of line bundles on surfaces whose Hom divisors have nonnegative canonical degree, the tensor product with a skyscraper sheaf has height exactly two, and the projections of skyscraper sheaves form a two-dimensional family of point-like objects in the orthogonal complement. We apply these tools to Orlov's rationality conjecture. A smooth projective complex surface is rational if its derived category has a full exceptional collection in which all members except possibly one are line bundles, or one that consists of at most three completely orthogonal blocks of arbitrary objects; we also obtain rationality in several cases with four blocks or with a hereditary component. If $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of the form $(M_i\boxtimes\mathcal O(a_i))$, then the $M_i$ with relative degrees of a fixed parity form a full exceptional collection on $S$; consequently $S$ is rational whenever $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. Finally, we show that the general case of the conjecture for surfaces is equivalent to the surjectivity and injectivity of two maps in Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: Galois lines for a canonical curve of genus 4, III: non-cyclic Galois lines
papers.abstract: Let $C \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be a canonical curve of genus $4$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. For a line $l \subset \mathbb{P}^3$, we consider the projection $\pi_l: C \to \mathbb{P}^1$ from $l$ and the induced extension of function fields $\pi_l^*: k(\mathbb{P}^1)\hookrightarrow k(C)$. A line $l$ is called an \emph{$S_3$-line} (resp. a \emph{$K_4$-line}) if the extension $k(C)/\pi_l^*(k(\mathbb{P}^1))$ is Galois and its Galois group is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_3$ on three letters (resp. the Klein four-group $K_4$). We prove that the number of $S_3$-lines (resp.\ $K_4$-lines) is at most $10$ (resp.\ $15$).

papers.title: Gauss--Bonnet theorem for o-minimal surfaces with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between topology and curvature of surfaces definable in an o-minimal structure. Our main result is a Gauss--Bonnet-type formula for closed (not necessarily compact) definable surfaces with finitely many singular points, expressing the Euler characteristic in terms of the total Gaussian curvature, the local densities at the singular points, and the density at infinity. As consequences, we obtain an inequality for definable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities and, for complex algebraic curves, a formula and an inequality relating the Euler characteristic, the total curvature, the multiplicities at the singular points and the degree.

papers.title: General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
papers.abstract: We present, for the first time, local Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields carrying $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $\Phi_{\mu^1[{\hat{s}_1}],\mu^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., \mu^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ using the BRST procedure with both the complete operator $Q$ and incomplete $Q_c$ BRST operators. Starting from a description of bosonic mixed-antisymmetric higher-spin fields in terms of an auxiliary Fock space associated with a special Poincare module, we realize a conversion of the initial operator constraint system into a system of first-class operator constraints. For this purpose, we find, for the first time, by means of Verma module the auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra, to be isomorphic due to Howe duality to $so(k,k)$ algebra, and containing the subsystem of second-class operators in terms of new oscillator variables forming the Fock module. An unconstrained (with $Q$) and constrained (with $Q_c$ and BRST invariant algebraic constraints) gauge Lagrangian formulations with equivalent dynamics, but different configuration spaces are found. We outline within $Q_c$-approach the concept of consistent local cubic interactions and evaluate the candidate structure of cubic vertices involving $p\geq 3$ copies of interacting massless mixed-antisymmetric fields.

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

papers.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
papers.abstract: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

papers.title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
papers.abstract: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important r\^ole in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.

papers.title: Gradient structures on metric measure spaces
papers.abstract: This work develops a theory of finite-rank gradients on metric measure spaces where the reference measure and the measure used to integrate gradients may be mutually singular. Examples include local trees, RCD spaces, sub-Riemannian manifolds, the harmonic Sierpiński gasket, and the Liouville Brownian motion.

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 2
papers.abstract: Ostrik classified fusion categories over $\mathbb C$ with two simple objects. We recover the two possible Grothendieck rings from sphericalization and central induction. For a candidate rule $X^2=1+nX$, the dimension divisibility of Etingof, Nikshych and Ostrik forces one lift of $X$ to satisfy the same rule in the sphericalization. The induction matrix then expresses $-n\dim(X)$ as the sum of two roots of unity. Taking a conjugate gives $n\leq 1$. Both rings occur.

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 3
papers.abstract: Ostrik classified the pivotal fusion categories of rank three. We show that every complex fusion category of rank three admits a spherical structure and recover the five Grothendieck rings. Both steps use the mass at twist one in the Drinfeld center. For an irreducible cubic codegree polynomial, Galois averaging in the sphericalization determines the first six moments of the squared twist.
