For a spherical category, the first two moments give a single inequality that excludes all the remaining rings outside the list. The rank-specific descent theorem we use from the literature is Ostrik's theorem for a quadratic factor.

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 4
papers.abstract: Every complex fusion category of rank four admits a spherical structure. Together with the pivotal classification of Dong, Palcoux and Plessis, this gives exactly fifteen Grothendieck rings. We prove sphericality by comparing the ordinary ring with the signed ring of the sphericalization. Formal codegrees and moments of central twists bound the dimension of a putative counterexample. An exact search leaves two signed Casimir polynomials for one ordinary ring. Both violate the same moment inequality. For the six rings with a non-self-dual simple, we also give a direct classification by central induction and twist moments.

papers.title: Hadamard matrices of orders 668, 716, 892, 1132, 1244, 1388, 1436, 1676, 1772, 1916, 1948 and 1964
papers.abstract: We construct Hadamard matrices of orders 668, 716, 892, 1132, 1244, 1388, 1436, 1676, 1772, 1916, 1948 and 1964, the twelve multiples of 4 below 2000 for which none was known, and a second, inequivalent matrix of order 668. Five come from the Goethals–Seidel array with circulant blocks invariant under a multiplier group, four from the width-4 bordered array of Wallis and Whiteman, and four from bordered Goethals–Seidel arrays of widths 12, 20 and 28 whose corner is itself a Hadamard matrix. To our knowledge borders wider than 4 with a Hadamard corner are new; the first two arrays are classical. The four matrices with a border of width 4, of orders 668, 716, 1676 and 1772, are instances of a theorem of Miyamoto on Hadamard matrices of order $8m+4$, which Seberry and Yamada restated with their M-structures; the matrices to which the theorem applies were found here by computer search. The searches differ greatly in size. Those for the wider borders formed at most about $2^{44}$ pairs of candidate blocks. Those for orders 716 and 668 with a border of width 4, made with no multiplier group, formed about $2^{66}$ and $2^{59}$, and these two matrices, that of order 716 above all, are results of large-scale computation more than of a new construction. With these matrices, a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ is known for every $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $n\le 2000$.

papers.title: Hecke monoids, their homomorphisms and parabolicity
papers.abstract: One of the motivations of this work was the rather mysterious commutative submonoid of parabolic elements in any Hecke monoid of finite type, discovered by the first author and D. Kazhdan. To understand it, we introduce the class of (weakly) parabolic homomorphisms, which map parabolic elements to parabolic elements. The most prominent ones are those we call parabolic projections. We prove that products of parabolic elements can be described explicitly in terms of these remarkable homomorphisms. We also use them to find all pairs of commuting idempotents in Hecke monoids and prove that the number of such pairs in finite types miraculously depends only on the rank and satisfies a Fibonacci-like recurrence. We also introduce the class of locally injective homomorphisms. As a major step towards the classification of injective homomorphisms, we find all locally injective connected homomorphisms between Hecke monoids of types A, B and D and identify, albeit conjecturally, the injective ones. As a surprising byproduct of our study of parabolic and injective homomorphisms, we describe all homomorphisms between Hecke monoids. This gives hope that the classification of injective ones is achievable.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy. For nef, relatively ample line bundles over finitely generated fields, this energy is bounded below for almost every complex or nonarchimedean local-field realization of fixed polarized global model data, outside one null set common to the entire relative metric class. The results include big non-semiample examples. For ample $L$ and smooth positively curved $\bar{H}$, the complex critical equation is the Calabi--Yau equation; at zero volume, projective bundles recover Donaldson's functional. We also study critical metrics and conjectural canonical heights defined by energy envelopes.

papers.title: Heisenberg vertex algebras and abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Here we construct spaces of coinvariants for Heisenberg vertex algebras on abelian varieties and show that these globalize to twisted $\mathscr{D}$-modules on moduli of abelian varieties. We recover the standard construction of these sheaves over the Torelli locus. As an example, in the case of commutative Heisenberg vertex algebras we show that the realization of coinvariants on curves as polynomial functions on one-forms extends to arbitrary abelian varieties. Similarly, we construct twisted coinvariants on the universal abelian variety and show that these recover the standard construction over the universal Jacobian.

papers.title: Holomorphic Floer theory I: exponential integrals in finite and infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: In the first of the series of papers devoted to our project ``Holomorphic Floer Theory" we discuss exponential integrals and related wall-crossing structures. We emphasize two points of view on the subject: the one based on the ideas of deformation quantization and the one based on the ideas of Floer theory. Their equivalence is a corollary of our generalized Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. In the case of exponential integrals this amounts to several comparison isomorphisms between local and global versions of de Rham and Betti cohomology. We develop the corresponding theories in particular generalizing Morse-Novikov theory to the holomorphic case. We prove that arising wall-crossing structures are analytic. As a corollary, perturbative expansions of exponential integrals are resurgent. Based on a careful study of finite-dimensional exponential integrals we propose a conjectural approach to infinite-dimensional exponential integrals. We illustrate this approach in the case of Feynman path integral with holomorphic Lagrangian boundary conditions as well as in the case of the complexified Chern-Simons theory. We discuss the arising perverse sheaf of infinite rank as well as analyticity of the corresponding ``Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure". We develop a general theory of quantum wave functions and show that in the case of Chern-Simons theory it gives an alternative description of the Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure based on the notion of generalized Nahm sum. We propose several conjectures about analyticity and resurgence of the corresponding perturbative series.

papers.title: Indecomposable representations of $C^{\infty}(S^1,\aff)$ on polynomial spaces over jet spaces
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite dimensional complex vector spaces \(\pn\), \(n \in \bn\), consisting of polynomials on \(\jnmc\), the space of \((n-1)\) jets at a fixed point \(t_0 \in S^1\) of \(C^\infty\) functions \(S^1 \to \bc\). The loop group \(C^\infty(S^1,\aff)\) of the affine group \(\aff\) acts naturally on \(\pn\) by an indecomposable linear representation. The space \(\pn\) is canonically isomorphic to the space of holomorphic sections of a certain line bundle over the loop space of the Riemann sphere. It has an intricate structure, leading to infinite families of combinatorial identities. In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for a polynomial on \(\jnmc\) to belong to \(\pn\). Furthermore, we give partial answers to several conjectures concerning \(\pn\).

papers.title: Integrality and polynomiality in Somos recurrences
papers.abstract: We prove that the standard Somos-$k$ sequence has a noninteger term for every $k\geq 8$ and give an explicit upper bound for the index of the first such term. We classify the three-term Somos recurrences with independent coefficients and all initial values equal to $1$ for which every term is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the recurrence coefficients. For each recurrence outside this classification, we bound the first index at which polynomiality fails and determine the reduced denominator at that index. We also show that every odd prime dividing a term of the standard Somos-$4$ sequence occurs to arbitrarily high valuation, with an exact formula along an explicit subsequence, and determine the $2$-adic valuation of every term.

papers.title: Invariant tensor dimensions as Hamburger moments
papers.abstract: For a self-dual object in a complex tensor category, we characterize the Hamburger moment property of its invariant tensor dimensions by a Cauchy--Schwarz inequality on sums of its tensor powers. Imposing the inequality on all pairs of objects determines the indecomposables in each block and the tensor rules of the unit block. For the additive group, the even invariant dimensions recover the Jordan type. In a finite tensor category of fusion type, Hamburger positivity for the projective cover of the unit forces unimodularity. If the identity and double dual are naturally isomorphic as additive functors, this positivity is equivalent to semisimplicity. A zero Cartan eigenvalue yields an explicit negative Hankel square in the unimodular case. We also prove semisimplicity of every finite categorification of the even $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Verlinde ring at every odd level. Finally, we give a Stieltjes criterion for $X\otimes X^*$ and a six-dimensional representation whose doubled sequence has a 42-atom representing measure through degree 83 and fails at degree 84.

papers.title: Irrational values of Dirichlet series with growing period
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a nonzero rational-valued function of period $D$. We count the exponents $2\le j\le s$ of prescribed parity for which $L_f(j)=\sum_{n\ge1}f(n)n^{-j}$ is irrational. For fixed $0<\eta<1$ our lower bound of order $\sqrt{s\log\log s/(D\log(sD))}$ has explicit constants and holds simultaneously for all $D\le s^{1-\eta}$ and all such $f$. For the real and imaginary parts of the quartic character modulo five we improve the previous lower-bound coefficient at even exponents by a factor of $2/\sqrt3$.

papers.title: Irrational values of Dirichlet series with periodic coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a nonzero rational-valued function of period $D$, and write $L_f(j)=\sum_{n\ge1} f(n)n^{-j}$. For either prescribed parity we give an explicit lower bound of order $\sqrt{s\log\log s/\log s}$ for the number of exponents $2\le j\le s$ of that parity for which $L_f(j)$ is irrational. The bound is uniform in $f$ for fixed $D$. It applies, for example, to every nonzero rational projection of a quartic Dirichlet character modulo five. If $f$ is even or odd, at most $D-1$ exponents $j\ge2$ of the matching parity give zero. The nonzero values at distinct exponents of that parity are linearly independent over the algebraic numbers.

papers.title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
papers.abstract: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

papers.title: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_{\alpha}(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $\nu(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $\alpha\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_{\alpha}(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

papers.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
papers.abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

papers.title: Maximizing the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue of Simple Pentagons
papers.abstract: We prove that among all simple pentagons of prescribed area—including non-convex pentagons and pentagons with straight interior angles—the regular pentagon uniquely maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Laplacian up to congruence. The proof separates naturally into two regimes. For pentagons having at least one reflex or straight interior angle, the number of strictly convex vertices is at most four; conformal mapping from the unit disk together with a Schwarz–Christoffel and Blaschke-product estimate yields the uniform bound $|P|\mu_1(P) < 10.34$, strictly below the regular-pentagon value $|R|\mu_1(R) > 10.35335$. For strictly convex pentagons, normalizing a maximum-area vertex triangle reduces the problem to a four-dimensional shape chart coupled with a unimodular metric matrix. Combining covariance bounds, explicit polynomial trial functions, conic duality for pairs of trial functions, and Bernstein-basis branch-and-bound, we confine every potential maximizer to an explicit neighborhood of the regular pentagon in vertex Fourier coordinates. Because the first positive eigenspace of the regular pentagon is two-dimensional, we analyze both eigenfunctions simultaneously together with their first-order corrections to show that every nontrivial local deformation of the similarity class strictly decreases $|P|\mu_1(P)$. All finite-dimensional inequalities invoked in the proof are accompanied by independently verifiable rational and interval arithmetic certificates.

papers.title: Modularity of the factors of an automorphic tensor product
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field and let $\rho_1,\rho_2$ be two-dimensional $p$-adic representations of $G_F$ which are Lie-irreducible and potentially modular, each over its own extension. We prove the following: if $\rho_1\otimes\rho_2$ is attached to a regular L-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation $\Pi$ of $\GL_4(\A_F)$, then $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are modular and $\Pi\simeq\pi_1\boxtimes\pi_2$. This is a converse to Ramakrishnan's automorphy of the Rankin--Selberg product. The proof combines the descent of Hundley--Sayag from $\GL_4$ to $\GSpin_4$ with $L$-function arguments based on potential modularity. To pin down the weights of the factors we use the Galois representations attached to the adjoint lifts $\ad\pi_i'$ on $\GL_3$; this rules out factors of mixed parity.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of untwisted wild Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct moduli stacks of wild Riemann surfaces in the (pure) untwisted case, for any complex reductive structure group, and we define the corresponding (pure) wild mapping class groups.

papers.title: Morphisms and comorphisms of sites I -- Double categories of sites
papers.abstract: We arrange morphisms and comorphisms of sites as the horizontal and vertical cells of a double category of sites; using the formalism of extensions and restrictions of presheaves, we explains how one can define a sheafification double functor from this double category to the quintet double category of Grothendieck topoi. We describe properties of this double functor and recover some classical results of topos theory through a new notion of locally exact square, generalizing exact squares in the presence of topologies. We also describe a 2-comonad on $\Cat$ for which lax morphisms of coalgebras are morphisms of sites and colax morphisms are comorphisms of sites, explaining the arrangement as a double category.

papers.title: Non-existence of non-Eulerian irregular Diophantine quadruples
papers.abstract: A Diophantine quadruple $\{a,b,c,d\}$ with $a<b<c<d$ is irregular if $d\ne a+b+c+2abc+2\sqrt{(ab+1)(ac+1)(bc+1)}$. It is conjectured that there are none, and He and Togb\'e have recently given a proof that there are only finitely many, with $c<10^{338}$. We study the non-Eulerian irregular quadruples, those whose triple $\{a,b,c\}$ is not an Euler triple, that is, $c\ne a+b+2\sqrt{ab+1}$, and reduce them to nine explicit families. The families are defined by the degree of $\{a,b,c\}$ under canonical descent, by the position of the descent partner $d_-(a,b,c)$ relative to $a$ and $b$, by the shape of the iterated descent, and by explicit windows for the index of $z=\sqrt{cd+1}$ in two Pell sequences. In particular $c<10^{99}$, and $c<10^{79.71}$ when $z$ has an odd-index representation; for triples of degree one, $c<1.81\cdot10^{47}$. He and Togb\'e obtained $c<10^{162}$ for degree one and $c<10^{338}$ for higher degree. With the bound $c<4\cdot10^{48}$ for Euler triples of a companion paper, every irregular Diophantine quadruple has $c<10^{99}$. For each family we give exact finite tests, in integer arithmetic or with certified rational enclosures, whose success shows that a given triple of the family has no irregular extension. Running these tests over the families is a finite computation. The numerical verification of these remaining cases is in progress, and its results will be appended to the final version of the paper.

papers.title: Note on parallel transport of IHS manifolds of Kummer type
papers.abstract: We give a characterization of parallel transport operators for irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of Kummer type.

papers.title: Numerical evidence for the almost Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We report on encouraging numerical evidence for the almost Hadamard conjecture, stating that any local maximizer of the $1$-norm on $U_N$ must have all entries of modulus $1/\sqrt{N}$, or equivalently that every complex almost Hadamard matrix $H=\sqrt{N}\,U$ must be a complex Hadamard matrix, with computations at the key values $N=4,5$ arising from our attempts to both prove and disprove the conjecture, and adding to the previous abstract evidence.

papers.title: Observation cost of nonequilibrium in nonnormal networks: a matched exponent for an explicit four-state generator
papers.abstract: We consider detection of nonequilibrium from passive, causally scheduled snapshots of a stationary continuous-time Markov chain, with gaps between snapshots of at least $\tau$. False alarms must be controlled uniformly over every finite stationary detailed-balance chain observed through a deterministic labelling, with no restriction on hidden dimension, rates, stationary label law or mixing time. Aznagulov showed that for normal generators the optimal snapshot cost grows like $e^{2\gamma_{\rm irr}\tau}$, and that for nonnormal generators its exponent lies in a spectral window. For an explicit nonnormal four-state generator $Q_4$, with a real slow mode and residual damping $\beta$, we prove that $\tau^{-1}\log N^*\to2\gamma$, where $\gamma=(701-\sqrt{158761})/126\in(2,\beta)$ is a relaxation rate of an explicit reversible birth–death comparator; for $Q_4$ this exponent lies strictly inside the window $[2,2\beta]$. The comparator comes from an ordered-eigenfunction completion lemma: among $\pi$-reversible generators with a prescribed strictly monotone eigenfunction and eigenvalue, a birth–death generator maximizes the entire Dirichlet form. The upper bound uses symmetric two-lag scores whose stationary mean is nonpositive under every hidden reversible model, together with a positive-operator tilt lemma that gives the moment-generating bound $e^{32n\theta^2}$ for a deterministic number $n$ of dependent transitions, uniformly over the null class. We also show that the two-lag pair-law approximation exponent of $Q_4$ by hidden reversible models is $\gamma$, that the cost exponent $2\gamma$ holds uniformly over a four-parameter box of nonnormal deformations, and that it extends to interacting path families on $\{1,2,3,4\}^d$ built from tensor lifts. More generally, if $u$ has distinct entries and is an eigenvector of $Q$ and of its $L^2(\pi)$-adjoint with eigenvalue $-\lambda$, the exponent is $2\gamma^*$ whenever $\gamma^*<\beta$, where $\gamma^*$ is the restricted gap of the completion.

papers.title: Old and new Drinfeld cusp forms of level t in characteristic 2: the weights k = 2^m + 1
papers.abstract: Let q = 2, A = F_2[t], and let U_t be the Atkin operator on the space S_k(Gamma_0(t)) of Drinfeld cusp forms of level t. For every weight k = 2^m + 1 we prove that S_k(Gamma_0(t)) is the direct sum of its oldforms and its newforms, that k/2 is the largest slope of U_t, and that no oldform has slope k/2. This is Conjecture 1.2(3) of Bandini and Valentino, and their conjectured old/new decomposition, for this infinite family of weights in characteristic 2, where the known methods do not apply. We also obtain the characteristic polynomial of U_t in closed form in terms of that of the Hecke operator T_t in level one, and the bound: every slope of T_t on S_k(GL_2(A)) is at most J_m = (2^m - (-1)^m)/3. The proof rests on a combinatorial theorem: the leading principal minors of the Bandini-Valentino matrix are nonzero exactly at the Jacobsthal numbers; equivalently, the number of perfect matchings of the graph of nonempty subsets of {1, ..., m} joined when disjoint or nested is odd exactly when the number of vertices plus one is a Jacobsthal number.

papers.title: On automorphisms of symplectic varieties acting trivially on the second cohomology group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group of automorphisms acting trivially on the torsion-free part of the integral second cohomology on a primitive symplectic variety is a locally trivial deformation invariant. We exhibit some examples of this invariant.

papers.title: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$.
  We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $\chi\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $\pi_{\chi,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $\pi_{\chi}=\operatorname{ind}_P^G\chi$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(\chi\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(\pi_{\chi})\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $\chi$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $\pi_{\chi,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(\chi\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $\chi$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(\pi_{\chi})\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

papers.title: On sequential ideal measurements in the exceptional Jordan algebra
papers.abstract: Real, complex and quaternionic quantum theory have one exceptional relative, the Albert algebra $H_3(\mathbb O)$, which single-system reconstructions leave standing. Sequences of measurements on a single system can still tell it apart, provided the measurements are ideal. A yes–no test is ideal if it disturbs the state no more than its answer requires, as under the projection postulate. Ideal tests of finitely many pure states of $H_3(\mathbb O)$ are then matched by ideal measurements on a real, complex or quaternionic Hilbert space of any dimension exactly when those states fail to generate the algebra. When they generate it, an ideal Hilbert-space model matching every sequence from even one starting state would yield a faithful representation of the algebra and its Jordan product by operators, which Albert ruled out in 1934. Three states never generate it; whether four do is decided by one number, proportional to a squared octonion associator. Even when four do, the difference is slow to show: from the maximally mixed state, a random choice between two quaternionic qutrits matches every sequence of up to six outcomes, and only at seven is every Hilbert-space model excluded. If the tests need not be ideal, then for any finite set of tests a finite-dimensional quantum device with sharp answers matches every sequence, of any length.

papers.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract:
Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincar\'e polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$.
  Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$.
  For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

papers.title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
papers.abstract: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$. We prove that $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)<\infty$ if and only if $\exp(G)$ is odd and greater than $3$, and the largest invariant factor of $G$ occurs at least twice. In that case, \[ \mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=\max\{\mathrm{rk}(G),\mathrm{rk}_3(G)+2\}. \] Specializing to $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=2$ recovers the classical result of Bauer, Catanese and Grunewald: the finite abelian Beauville surface groups are precisely $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ with $n>1$ and $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Although the Beauville dimension has a geometric origin, our proof is entirely group-theoretic and combinatorial.

papers.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

papers.title: On the size of the fibers of a morphism of algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: Let u be a morphism of algebraic varieties. Given m integer or infinite, we prove that the set of points whose fiber has size m is a constructible set.

papers.title: On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.

papers.title: On Word Representations and Embeddings in Complex Matrices
papers.abstract: Embeddings of word structures into matrix semigroups provide a natural bridge between combinatorics on words and linear algebra. However, low-dimensional matrix semigroups impose strong structural restrictions on possible embeddings. Certain finitely generated groups admit faithful representations in SL(2, C) and other similar matrix groups. On the other hand, it is known that the product of two free semigroups on two generators cannot be embedded into the 2x2 complex matrices. In this paper we study embeddings of word structures into low-dimensional matrix semigroups over the complex numbers and develop new techniques for constructing word representations of the Euclidean Bianchi groups. These representations provide a symbolic framework and a natural first step towards analysing fundamental decision problems in 2x2 matrix semigroups.

papers.title: Parameterised complexity of graph homomorphism to odd cycles
papers.abstract: A nonbipartite graph has an odd-cycle core precisely when it maps to its shortest odd cycle. Core recognition and homomorphism to an input odd cycle are both XNLP-complete for the width of a supplied path decomposition, XALP-complete for the width of a supplied tree decomposition, and W[SAT]-hard and in W[P] for feedback vertex number. Hardness persists on connected, 2-degenerate $N$-vertex sources of girth $\Omega(N^{1-\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$. Our reduction encodes lists by cycles sharing an edge. On inputs with an edge it increases treewidth and feedback vertex number by exactly two. Lean 4 checks this structural transfer. For feedback edge number $r$, we compute the exact circular chromatic number in $2^{O(r)}$ time up to polynomial factors, which gives the same upper bound for both decision problems.

papers.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
papers.abstract: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.

papers.title: PHP decompositions and primitivity of group rings
papers.abstract: We show that every countable group $G$ that has Ozawa's property $\rm PHP$ and contains a non-abelian free subgroup has the following property: the group ring $KG$ is primitive for any field $K$. As a consequence, we greatly extend the previously existing results on the primitivity of group rings. New examples include linear groups and groups of homeomorphisms of the Cantor set. Along the way, we prove that the class of groups with $\rm PHP$ enjoys some permanence properties that are of independent interest.

papers.title: Pointwise Correlations of Quadratic Form Values and Splitting Semigroups
papers.abstract: Under the stated analytic inputs, we establish the fixed-shift pair asymptotics predicted by Smilansky for the ordinary values of \(x^2+dy^2\), \(d=1,2,3,4,7\). In particular, the number of \(n\le X\) for which both \(n\) and \(n+1\) are sums of two squares is asymptotic to \(X/(2\log X)\). For primitive positive definite binary forms of fixed discriminants \(\Delta_i=f_i^2D\) sharing one negative fundamental discriminant \(D\), we count values admitting coprime coordinates. Replacing either form within its respective genus preserves the leading binary count, with a relative logarithmic saving through an independent classical route. Under the recent analytic inputs we give an explicit mixed leading term with relative \(o(1)\), including different fixed conductors in that one field, and no class-number divisor. The central mechanism is a shared comparison between sparse indicators and arithmetic models retaining every surviving congruence character. Following Walsh's proposed indicator extension, we supply the models, local factors and a uniform reflected-target argument, using the recent zero-free and weighted-dilation theorems of OpenAI. Applications to fixed subgroup restrictions and prime-coset self-sums give target-uniform asymptotics with logarithmic savings and exact eventual congruence criteria. They include prime support \(1\pmod{12}\) on targets \(2\pmod{12}\) and prime support \(3\pmod4\) on even targets. All counts concern numerical values without coordinate or ideal multiplicities.

papers.title: Pointwise representation counts for Eisenstein restricted sums
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) consist of the positive integers supported on primes \(1\bmod 3\), including \(1\). We count distinct ordered representations \(n=a+b\) for \(n\equiv2\bmod6\) and \(n=a+3b\) for \(n\equiv4\bmod6\), with \(a,b\in A\). In either family prescribe an interval of length \(H\) centered at \(x\) for one actual summand. Put \(M=\min(x,n-x)\). For every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), if \(H\le M\) and \(H^3\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}M\), the count has order \(HJ(n)/\log n\) for every sufficiently large admissible \(n\). Here \(J(n)\) is the product of \((p-1)/(p-2)\) over the odd primes \(p\equiv2\bmod3\) dividing \(n\). In particular, central windows of width \(n^\theta\) are allowed for \(2/3<\theta<1\), and windows at a prescribed small summand of size comparable to their width are allowed for \(1/2<\theta<1\). The lower bound combines angular Hecke estimates with a sieve that prescribes small split factors in both summands.

papers.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
papers.abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. B\'erczi and Feh\'er conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Power-saving bounds for balanced radical triples via small Pell discriminants
papers.abstract: For $0<\lambda\leq 1$, let $\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}(N)$ be the set of integers $n\leq N$ for which $\mathrm{rad}(n(n+1)(2n+1))<(2n+1)^{\lambda}$. The elementary radical-box estimate gives $|\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}(N)|\ll N^{\lambda/3+\varepsilon}$. We prove a strict power-saving refinement of this exponent: there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $|\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}(N)|\ll_{\lambda,\varepsilon}N^{\lambda/3-C\lambda^{3}+\varepsilon}$. The argument uses Diao's uniform bound for the number of small fundamental solutions to Pell equations, together with a squarefree-kernel transfer for the three unit-difference equations, a fixed-support radical-box lemma, and a three-branch dyadic optimization. We also formulate the resulting estimate for high-quality values and for Chinese-remainder orbits, and quantify the variable-right-hand-side obstruction to a direct extension to arbitrary abc triples. No assertion of the abc or Szpiro conjecture is used, and no pointwise abc inequality is claimed. The only non-elementary external input is Diao's Theorem 1.3 in arXiv:2610.28001v1, whose statement and preprint status are recorded explicitly.

papers.title: Prime Knots with Augmentation-Rank Gaps at Unbounded Bridge Number
papers.abstract: We construct explicit braid families containing infinitely many distinct hyperbolic prime knots of each bridge number \(b=5,6\) and each sufficiently large \(b\), with complex augmentation rank at most \(b-1\) and meridional rank \(b\). Alternating-group colorings force \(b\) meridional generators, while two fixed meridian words let a local rank-one obstruction persist as the braid grows. An oriented diagram isotopy realizes the associated two-cusped exteriors as fillings of a single three-cusped exterior. Rigorous interval certificates establish hyperbolicity of that exterior and the two small-bridge exteriors used in the filling argument.

papers.title: Quasimonomial Monge--Amp\`ere equations for big classes
papers.abstract: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case. We also obtain continuity of solutions as numerical classes vary in the big cone. This extends previous results of Boucksom--Jonsson and Dervan--Reboulet, and gives the first uniqueness results in the big case. Our approach relies on convex geometry and Okounkov bodies, without involving non-Archimedean pluripotential theory or test configurations.

papers.title: Ramanujan primes and primes of exponent one in products of consecutive integers
papers.abstract: Let \(M(L)\) be the minimum number of primes occurring to exponent one in a product of \(L\) consecutive positive integers. Assuming the ordinary \(abc\) conjecture, we prove that, for all sufficiently large \(L\), \(M(L)\) equals the number of Ramanujan primes at most \(L\). Thus the least length threshold guaranteeing \(k\) such primes is the \(k\)th Ramanujan prime for every sufficiently large \(k\). The identity holds unconditionally if the last entry is at most \(\exp(c(\log L)^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log\log L})\), for an absolute \(c>0\). We determine the limiting count at every fixed ratio of the starting offset to the length. We also prove unconditionally that the factorial count can exceed the minimum by an unbounded amount, and that ordinary primes contain arbitrarily long runs of consecutive non-Ramanujan primes.

papers.title: Rigid affine cones over singular del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We completely determine the existence of anticanonical polar cylinders in quasi-smooth log del Pezzo surfaces of index one.

papers.title: Schubert Cox Rings and Root Operators
papers.abstract: We identify the Cox ring of every Schubert variety in a symmetrizable Kac--Moody partial flag variety with an upper cluster algebra whose frozen variables are not inverted. The construction also applies to Bott--Samelson varieties for arbitrary words and to their normal projective birational contractions that preserve the standard affine chart. A line-bundle recursion determines the boundary coefficients of the exchange relations. In this mutation class, each nonzero positive simple-root operator and each nonzero stabilizing negative simple-root operator acts in a suitable seed as a monomial times a partial derivative in one frozen variable. Consequently, a single theta basis describes the root filtrations on all divisorial section spaces. We compute the facets of its regular cone from the word and the surviving divisors. The leading terms of the root operators yield tropical formulas for finite-type Levi crystals and polyhedral formulas for branching multiplicities. We obtain formulas for adjoint sections and extend the adapted root charts to projective horospherical varieties with free class group under a simply connected semisimple group.

papers.title: Sharp packing bounds for Poly-5 and Handy-Octs
papers.abstract: On the 89-square Poly-5 board, distinct pentominoes can cover at most 26 of the 28 boundary squares and 56 of the 60 exterior unit edges. Both maxima occur in a full tiling. For the five Handy-Octs octiamonds, the least area of a convex triangular-grid enclosure is 43 unit triangles. There is one optimal enclosure and it has precisely five packings, up to lattice symmetries. We prove the bounds by finite enumeration.

papers.title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
papers.abstract: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Pl\"ucker embedding. The rotating staircases split into many linkage classes and we give some examples.

papers.title: Slope stability for normal varieties
papers.abstract: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.

papers.title: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
papers.abstract: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

papers.title: Spectral measure blowup for Hadamard subfactors
papers.abstract: We study the spectral measures of the Hadamard subfactors coming from the deformed Fourier matrices $F_X\otimes_QF_Y$. After preliminaries on small-index graphs and exceptional root measures, we express the law through a Gram matrix over a compact abelian group, interpret this as an abelian covering, and compute the moment growth. At index 6 the generic law comes from the honeycomb and kagome lattices, and finite cases correspond to Eisenstein ideals. Circulant families at square index give planar random walk laws. We locate the first Jacobi defect and construct finite-depth laws with arbitrarily long generic moment sequences.

papers.title: Spectral outliers of self-coupled covariance matrices with exact zero weights
papers.abstract: We study the right spectral outliers of $M_d=n^{-1}A_dDA_d^{\mathsf T}$, where the columns of $A_d$ are drawn from a Gaussian mixture with a fixed-dimensional signal subspace and each diagonal weight $D_{\ell\ell}=h_{b_\ell}(g_\ell)$ is a function of the class label and of the low-dimensional Gaussian coordinates of the same sample. The effective outlier theory of Ben Arous, Gheissari, Huang and Jagannath for such self-coupled matrices assumes that the weights do not accumulate at zero, which excludes hard gates such as the derivative of a rectified linear unit. Assuming $h_b(g)\in\{0\}\cup[\tau,M]$, we prove that exact zero weights do not change the positive right-outlier equation. The proof deletes inactive columns before any linearization, keeps their random normalization, and applies the invertible-weight theory to the exact conditional mark law of the active samples; we show, by conditioning on the marks, that this theory extends to non-Gaussian fixed-dimensional marks. The limiting spectrum acquires the atom $(1-\phi\pi)_+$ at zero, while positive outliers are the roots of a $q\times q$ determinant. We obtain multiplicity-preserving eigenvalue counts, absence of spurious right outliers, a projected-eigenvector normalization, an invariant-subspace formula at repeated roots, and the exact finite-dimensional kernel.

papers.title: Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas
papers.abstract: In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.

papers.title: Spontaneous X-rays Exclude Gaussian Covariant Classical–Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: In classical-quantum gravity the metric stays classical, and complete positivity ties the decoherence of matter to the diffusion of the metric. The covariant theory of Oppenheim and collaborators is viable by its authors' assessment, which does not evaluate the matter noise at keV frequencies. That noise conflicts with XENONnT's search for spontaneous X-rays, by two arguments that fail under different escapes. First, the covariant diffusion makes the conformal mode dynamical; near the light cone slow matter feels it through its rest mass, while Maxwell's equations do not. For translation-invariant kernels and every diffusion weight that is Lorentz invariant in the scalar sector, whatever its regulator or running in $p^2$, the trade-off forces matter noise $s\geq\tfrac23|f|/p^2$ on a conserved near-null source, in units of the Diósi-Penrose kernel. Where Newton's law is tested, $|f|=1$ and $\int s\,dp^2\geq9.2$, against a limit of $7.7\times10^{-8}$ from our likelihood fit to the published XENONnT spectrum: an exclusion by $\geq1.1\times10^{8}$ (median expected $6.6\times10^{7}$). A frame in the scalar weight evades it. Second, general relativity's response to a conserved near-null source has a light-cone pole, which is purely tensor. The resulting bound holds for every positive diffusion weight, with or without a frame. It assumes general relativity's tensor propagator at keV momenta, but no transfer of static tests; an atom's Coulomb field gives the tensor source an order-one share. The margin, $1.7\times10^{9}$ (median expected $9.8\times10^{8}$), is an estimate, not a bound. At linear order, a classical theory that survives both needs a frame or a non-perturbative mass above $(0.34~\mu\mathrm{m})^{-1}$ in the scalar sector, and a tensor sector off the light cone, or with a form factor, at keV momenta, or a coupling blind to the atom's stress; or a frame carried by the matter coupling, or possibly by the state of an extra field (open); or noise outside the Gaussian class, which for a Poisson record of jumps must deliver its keV emission in multi-photon bursts.

papers.title: State complexity of rare-switching tracking: universal bounds and sharp counter tradeoffs
papers.abstract: We study the number of internal states required to track a symmetric binary Markov signal observed through a fixed binary symmetric channel. For homogeneous recursive controllers with independent private randomization, a posterior-covering converse gives the sharp leading state coefficient in the iterated nearly-Bayes-optimal limit, uniformly over controller kernels and stationary recurrent mixtures. At a fixed relative excess error, we also determine the exact leading coefficient within symmetric observation-driven birth–death counters with a prescribed sign decoder. Their acceptance probabilities may vary across states and tend to zero with the switching probability. A stationary flow argument links a confidence barrier to actual switch-time mass, and a discounted passage estimate controls repeated switching. For general MAP-decoded controllers, a point certificate for the same posterior covers shows that this counter coefficient is optimal at every fixed relative excess above an explicit threshold depending only on the channel; below that threshold the general frontier remains open, and the gap is narrowed. State cardinality is the resource; no thermodynamic work claim is made.

papers.title: Sums of three composite triangular numbers
papers.abstract: A triangular number T_k = k(k+1)/2 is composite for every k >= 3, the only non-composite ones being 0, 1 and 3. We ask which integers are sums of three composite triangular numbers, a restricted form of Gauss's Eureka theorem; equivalently, when 8n+3 is a sum of three squares none of which is 1, 9 or 25. We prove that every integer n > 194 is a sum of three composite triangular numbers, with at most three possible exceptions, all larger than 8.4*10^9. Such exceptions can occur only if Tatuzawa's form of Siegel's theorem, with eps = 1/20, has an exceptional discriminant -N*, and then only for 8n+3 in {N*, 9N*, 25N*}. Up to 8.4*10^9 the integers that are not such sums are exactly 41 explicit values, the largest being 194. Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis these 41 values are the complete list. The proof combines an elementary lemma, a union bound for the representations that use a forbidden square, the class number formula for sums of three squares, Tatuzawa's theorem, and explicit bounds for a divisor-type function. The analytic range begins at 8n+3 = 3.4561*10^10 and overlaps the computed range by a factor 1.944. The computed range is certified by two independent algorithms, supplied as ancillary files together with a verifier for every constant.

papers.title: Supersingular Ekedahl-Oort strata and Oort's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}_g$ be the moduli space over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $g$-dimensional principally polarised abelian varieties, where $p$ is a prime. We show that if $g$ is even and $p\geq 5$, then every geometric generic member in the maximal supersingular Ekedahl-Oort stratum in $\mathcal{A}_g$ has automorphism group $\{ \pm 1\}$. This confirms Oort's conjecture in the case of $p\geq 5$ and even $g$. We also separately prove Oort's conjecture for $g=4$ and $p >2$.

papers.title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $\pi$. We show that $\pi^2 = p\,\alpha_*$ for a unique automorphism $\alpha$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $\pi^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,\chi))$, where $\chi$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

papers.title: Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space
papers.abstract: Symmetry-based structures have advanced molecular spectroscopy and quantum information science, yet connections between these fields remain largely unexplored. We construct a phase space theory of a molecule by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as the quotient of orientations and normal coordinates by the molecule's point group. The various combinations of how these three degrees of freedom transform under symmetries organize a molecule's states into molecular species, and we show that each species is defined by a particular absolutely maximally entangled (AME) carrier state, or, for 45 species, by a two-dimensional space of them. Up to local unitaries and the order of the sectors, molecular species realize 21 AME states across 75 point groups: a product state, four maximally entangled pairs, and 16 genuinely tripartite states. A Fourier transform on the quotient relates orientation and angular-momentum descriptions while preserving these carrier states. We propose an example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of $\mathrm{CaOCH_3}$.

papers.title: The alternating sum of reciprocal Fibonacci cubes is irrational
papers.abstract: We prove that the alternating sum of the reciprocal cubes of the Fibonacci numbers is irrational. The result extends to the Lucas sequences of the first kind associated with real quadratic units greater than one, including the Pell numbers. For every such sequence and every fixed positive integer $k$, the reciprocal cubes with indices $k,2k,3k,\ldots$, taken with signs $+,-,+,\ldots$, also have an irrational sum.

papers.title: The Assumption Package of the Yang–Mills Construction: Formal Definitions and Derivations
papers.abstract: This is a companion document for the conditional mass‑gap theorem for four‑dimensional pure Yang‑Mills theory. We collect formal definitions and derivations for the full set of external hypotheses (RG1–RG5, UV1, PH1–PH3, AN1, Y1–Y4, B1, C1) employed in the lattice‑based construction. A volume‑consistent revised condition RG4' is established, repairing a potential volume‑divergence issue in the original formulation. Several algebraic identities are cross‑validated against the Lean 4 formal‑verification repository. We emphasize that this package of assumptions is not sufficient to prove the mass gap: counterexamples satisfy all these hypotheses while having zero mass gap. Three further open mathematical components remain required for the mass‑gap result: a volume‑uniform log‑Sobolev inequality, an Euclidean‑to‑Hamiltonian correspondence theorem, and a non‑perturbative Callan–Symanzik Ward identity implementing dynamical mass generation.

papers.title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
papers.abstract: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

papers.title: The Dimension-Degree Boundary for Gaussian Moment Vanishing
papers.abstract: We classify complex polynomials of degree at most three in three independent standard real Gaussian variables whose positive moments all vanish. Up to a complex orthogonal linear change of coordinates and a nonzero scalar, every such polynomial has one-sided circular support or belongs to a single exceptional orbit. For every fixed polynomial $Q$, its mixed moments $\mathbb E[QP^m]$ vanish whenever $m>3\deg Q$, and the coefficient three is optimal. The proof extracts a Gaussian coordinate in which the polynomial is affine linear, then classifies that family using formal stationary frames and analytic period estimates. Combining this ternary-cubic result with Wilson's two-variable theorem, Liu's quadratic theorem and Long's counterexamples gives the exact dimension-degree boundary for the Gaussian Moments Conjecture: the implication from pure-moment vanishing to eventual mixed-moment vanishing holds universally precisely when there are at most two variables, the degree is at most two, or there are three variables and the degree is at most three. We reproduce the all-order moment identities for the two minimal failures.

papers.title: The equilateral triangle maximises the first Steklov eigenvalue among triangles
papers.abstract: Let $\sigma_1(T)$ be the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of a triangle $T$ and $L(T)$ its perimeter. Among triangles the equilateral triangle $E$ uniquely maximises $\sigma_1 L$. If the shortest and longest sides of $T$ have lengths $a\le b$, then $\sigma_1(E)L(E)-\sigma_1(T)L(T)\ge (b-a)/(2b)$. Since $|T|/L(T)^2$ is also maximal at $E$, the equilateral triangle uniquely maximises $\sigma_1\sqrt{|T|}$ as well. This settles the case $n=3$ of the Steklov analogue of the Pólya–Szegő conjecture for $n$-gons, for both normalisations. The extremal value satisfies $3.8724615957722\le \sigma_1(E)L(E)\le 3.8724615957734$. For side length one, $\sigma_1(E)=\sigma_2(E)<\sigma_3(E)=2\sqrt3<\sigma_4(E)$. Under displacement of the apex over a fixed unit base, the first two perimeter-normalised eigenvalues split linearly with equal and opposite slopes independent of direction. The proof is computer-assisted. Near $E$ we transplant the first eigenspace of $E$ affinely; away from $E$ the trial function $\cos(\pi x)$ suffices. We verify the finite matrix and interval inequalities in ball arithmetic.

papers.title: The exact FDR–FNR frontier and a separable gap under one-factor Gaussian dependence
papers.abstract: We determine the exact asymptotic trade-off between the false discovery rate and the false non-discovery rate in a two-group Gaussian model generated by one unobserved common factor of fixed strength. For fixed mixture weight, signal strength, equicorrelation, and false discovery target, the optimum over all randomized full-vector procedures converges to the lower convex envelope of the independent Gaussian threshold curve with effective signal \(\mu/\sqrt{1-\rho}\). Thus not observing the factor causes no additional asymptotic loss relative to the factor-revealed experiment. The converse reveals the factor and reduces exactly to an independent experiment. For achievability, factor estimation, a pathwise threshold-crossing bound, and random-denominator control yield an observable optimal rule with finite-sample FDR calibration. If the three model parameters are replaced by consistent estimates, a plug-in rule attains the same frontier with asymptotic FDR control. We also analyze the broad coordinate-local class \(\delta_{n,i}=f_{n,i}(X_i,A_n)\), where the functions may be nonidentical and dimension-dependent and the shared external seed is independent of the model. Every oracle supporting line lying strictly below the two trivial endpoint values has a positive asymptotic gap from this separable class; an analytic parameter choice certifies that such a line exists. For the constrained problem, the gap vanishes at every level exactly when the oracle frontier is the chord joining the reject-none and reject-all rules; otherwise it is strict at every level strictly between the two trivial endpoint levels. For this fixed rank-one Gaussian family, the first result exactly evaluates the compound frontier and the second proves existence of a strict gap from the stated coordinate-local class. Broad dependent model classes and the complete constrained separable frontier remain open.

papers.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

papers.title: The shortest word containing every permutation of ten symbols as a subsequence has length 83
papers.abstract: A word is universal for an alphabet if it contains every permutation of the alphabet as a subsequence. We prove that no word of length 82 is universal for ten symbols. Together with the known construction of length 83, this shows that the shortest universal word on ten symbols has length 83. The proof cuts a word at the copies of one symbol: universality is equivalent to complementary prefix and suffix conditions at consecutive copies. A counting argument confines a least frequent symbol to four, five, six or seven copies and excludes four. In the remaining cases, frequency tests reduce the possibilities to finitely many block templates, and machine-checked propositional refutations exclude every ordering of each. The computation also reproduces the nine-symbol value 66.

papers.title: The sum of the reciprocal Mersenne cubes is irrational
papers.abstract: The sum of the reciprocal cubes of the Mersenne numbers $2^n-1$ is irrational. More generally, for $|b|>1$ let $M_j(b)=\sum_{n\ge1}(b^n-1)^{-j}$. For every integer $b\ge2$, we prove that $1,M_1(b),M_2(b),M_3(b)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. These four numbers are also linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}(b)$ whenever $b$ is an algebraic integer with $|b|>1$ and every conjugate other than $b$ and $\bar b$ lies in the closed unit disk. This includes all Pisot and Salem numbers.

papers.title: The weight-three Lambert sum at the golden ratio is irrational
papers.abstract: For $|b|>1$, define the weight-three Lambert sum by $Z(b)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^2/(b^n-1)$. For an algebraic integer $b$ in this range, we prove that $Z(b)\notin\mathbb{Q}(b)$ if every conjugate outside the closed unit disk belongs to $\{b,\bar b\}$. This includes all Pisot and Salem bases. For a Salem base we bound the polynomial approximations even at conjugates on the unit circle, where the series diverges. At the golden ratio $\varphi=(1+\sqrt{5})/2$, the sum $Z(\varphi)$ lies outside $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and is therefore irrational. A nonreal example is $Z(1+i)\notin\mathbb{Q}(i)$.

papers.title: The Černý (1969) conjecture holds for quasi-Eulerian automata of degree one
papers.abstract: An automaton with $n$ states is quasi-Eulerian of degree $d$ if there are positive letter weights summing to one, a set $X$ of $d$ exceptional states and a further state $s$ such that every state outside $X\cup\{s\}$ receives total weight one and every edge that starts in $X$ ends in $X\cup\{s\}$. Berlinkov bounded the reset threshold of strongly connected synchronizing ones by $2^d(n-d+1)(n-1)$. We prove that every synchronizing quasi-Eulerian automaton of degree one has a reset word of length at most $(n-1)^2$, so the Černý (1969) conjecture holds for this family; the Černý automata belong to it and attain the bound. The same bound holds for every synchronizing automaton whose transition matrix, weighted by some positive, possibly irrational, letter weights, has a positive stationary vector that is constant on all states but one; for this family Berlinkov's bound was $2n(n-1)$. For synchronizing quasi-Eulerian automata of degree two, the bound holds whenever the automaton is not strongly connected, whenever its two exceptional states form a block of a congruence, and, for binary strongly connected automata, in $46$ of the $49$ configurations (up to renaming) of the edges at the two exceptional states. The key step in degree one is elementary: a shortest word that takes the exceptional state out of a set $K$ of states that contains it has length at most $|K|$, and one that takes it into a set $K$ that does not contain it has length at most $n-|K|$.

papers.title: Thermodynamic saturation and prescribed window barriers for Kleinian-code graded spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate prescribed graded-window dimensions for Kleinian-code characters, motivated by the four-leg construction of a subexponential 3-SAT algorithm, but without claiming new admissible algebraic operators. For every compact $J\Subset(0,\infty)$, we prove, uniformly for isotropic additive codes $S\subset K^m$, $$ \rho_{\mathrm{win}}(V_S;h,\lambda)\geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\eta_J-C_Jm^{-1/2}, $$ whenever $h/m\in J$ and $2^\lambda\leq\dim(V_S)_h$, where $\eta_J>0$ is specified by the proof but has not yet been evaluated as a certified numerical constant for any given compact interval. The fixed-density proof combines the central-window inequality, sectorwise thermodynamic estimates based on the isotropic local weight bound, finite-length concentration, and certified interval arithmetic (Arb, cross-checked with mpmath.iv) for specified sign inequalities. These numerical certificates do not formalize the complete proof. No concavity or convergence assumption on the code-weight spectrum is needed. For additive codes of 2-rank at most $m$, we also prove that the maximally encoded prescribed-window cost converges uniformly to $1/\sqrt{2}$ as $h/m\to\infty$, with two-sided explicit errors of order $O(\sqrt{m/h}+(mh)^{-1/4})$ for admissible $h\geq 15m$ and $mh\geq 4000$. These are statements about window dimensions, not intrinsic matrix ranks or implementations within a SAT algorithm.

papers.title: Three Roles and One Bit: All Optimal Tables and Equality Graphs
papers.abstract: We study a randomized one-bit fingerprint for distinguishing graphs on a common labeled vertex set. Each vertex independently receives one of three roles according to a common probability distribution. A symmetric Boolean table assigns bits to pairs of roles, and the fingerprint is the parity of these bits over the graph's edges. We prove that, for every $n \geq 4$, the optimal worst-case detection probability over all symmetric Boolean tables and role distributions is exactly $8/27$. Every optimal distribution is uniform. For $n \geq 5$, we classify exactly 21 optimal tables with fixed role labels; one additional table is optimal when $n=4$. We characterize all graphs attaining the minimum, up to isomorphism and isolated vertices: the four-cycle $C_4$ occurs for every optimal table, while the three-vertex path $P_3$ occurs additionally for 15 tables. For the canonical optimal table, we establish that the second distinct minimum is $80/243$ when $n \geq 6$, attained precisely by $K_{2,4}$ with possible isolated vertices. For $n=4,5$, the second minimum is $1/3$. Our analytic proofs use homogeneous quadratic forms over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_4$, supported by reproducible exhaustive computations. The results also apply to differences of interlacement graphs associated with double-occurrence words.

papers.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
papers.abstract:
We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures.
  Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

papers.title: Torsion cycles on Fermat varieties
papers.abstract:
A theorem of Manin and Drinfeld states that any divisor of degree $0$ on the cusps of a modular curve is torsion in the Jacobian. An elegant proof of this result was provided by Elkik using mixed Hodge theory.
  Rohrlich proved a generalization of this to Fermat curves. In this paper we reprove his results along the lines of the work of Elkik. We then use the same methods to generalize it to higher Chow cycles. We introduce a notion of `ambient decomposability' - essentially cycles coming from the ambient ${\mathbb P}^{n+1}$ and the base field - and show that higher Chow cycles determined by coordinate sections are necessarily of this type.
  This is a revised and accepted version of the earlier manuscript of the same name and is to appear in Indagationes Mathematicae. The results are stronger than the results in the earlier manuscript.

papers.title: Total stability and Auslander-Reiten theory for Dynkin quivers
papers.abstract: This paper concerns stability functions for Dynkin quivers, in the generality introduced by Rudakov. We show that relatively few inequalities need to be satisfied for a stability function to be totally stable (i.e. to make every indecomposable stable). Namely, a stability function $\mu$ is totally stable if and only if $\mu(\tau V) < \mu(V)$ for every almost split sequence $0 \to \tau V \to E \to V \to 0$ where $E$ is indecomposable. These can be visualized as those sequences around the "border" of the Auslander-Reiten quiver.

papers.title: Towards a conformal field theory of critical percolation. II. Scalar responses and null identities
papers.abstract: We construct the scalar response to closing a small disk in critical site percolation on the triangular lattice. The response records how the obstacle changes every connection at a surrounding boundary. Its normalized cutoff error is of order r^(11/15), and an open-cutset argument gives its leading fusion with the density field in the complete-record norm. We identify the signed response in a domain with six alternating boundary tips and prove the level-two null identities against finite separated density, scalar, and stress insertions. These identities determine the mixed scalar–density four-point function. Assuming Camia and Feng’s asymptotic formula for one energy and two density insertions, we give their energy field a geometric interpretation as the normalized response to closing a small disk. The resulting correlation of two energies and two densities is the difference of a successive-bottleneck and an alternative-route contribution, and it changes sign. The second coefficient in the angularly averaged scalar–density collision defines a nonzero insertion Ψ of weights (77/96,77/96). Fixed stress contours and radial integrals give joint correlations of every fixed finite collection of separated Ψ insertions, with error O( \sum_i (r_i)^(1/2) ) at arbitrary relative extraction radii. We compute its two-point coefficient and signed two-obstacle connection asymptotics, including the leading stress term when the scalar sources collide in a two-density correlation. These results realize the known analytic conformal blocks through specified lattice observables. The construction uses the complete-record stress estimates and finite-hole density correlations of Paper I.

papers.title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
papers.abstract: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.

papers.title: Tropical Lagrangian coamoebae and generalized dimer models
papers.abstract: We study the coamoebae of Lagrangian submanifolds of $(\mathbb{C}^\times)^n$, specifically how the combinatorics of their degenerations encodes the homological algebra of mirror coherent sheaves. Concretely, to a minimal free resolution $F^\bullet$ of a module $M$ over $\mathbb{C}[z_1^{\pm 1}, \dotsc, z_n^{\pm 1}]$ we associate a simplicial complex $T(F^\bullet) \subset T^n$. We call $T(F^\bullet)$ a tropical Lagrangian coamoeba. We show that the discrete information in $F^\bullet$ can often be recovered from $T(F^\bullet)$, and that more generally $M$ is mirror to a certain constructible sheaf supported on $T(F^\bullet)$. The resulting interplay between coherent sheaves on $(\mathbb{C}^\times)^n$ and simplicial complexes in $T^n$ provides a higher-dimensional generalization of the spectral theory of dimer models in $T^2$, as well as a symplectic counterpart to the theory of brane brick models.

papers.title: Two shorter intervals of even Dirichlet beta values
papers.abstract: We prove that each of the sets $\{\beta(6),\beta(8),\ldots,\beta(66)\}$ and $\{\beta(8),\beta(10),\ldots,\beta(98)\}$ contains an irrational number. These sets contain $31$ and $46$ values, respectively, improving the previous intervals with the same lower endpoints, which contained $35$ and $52$ values.

papers.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

papers.title: Uniform intervals for irrational even beta values
papers.abstract: For every positive integer $q$, at least one of the Dirichlet beta values $\beta(2q+2),\beta(2q+4),\ldots,\beta(2\lfloor33q/2\rfloor)$ is irrational. This gives an explicit interval from every even starting index at least four. For every positive odd $m$, some even $s$ with $m+1\le s\le(299/20)m+C$ has $\beta(s)$ irrational, where $C$ is absolute. This reduces the previous upper-endpoint multiplier $18.58$ to $14.95$ up to a bounded additive term. For every odd $m\ge4{,}000{,}000{,}001$, the explicit endpoint $s<15m$ suffices.

papers.title: Uniform Spectral Gap and Stability for the Spin-2 Square-Lattice AKLT Model with Free Boundaries
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform spectral gap above the full ground space of the spin-2 AKLT Hamiltonian on every square-lattice rectangle with four free sides and both lengths at least two. The ground-space dimension grows exponentially with the perimeter. Starting from the classical hard-boundary coupling of Aronow and Lopatto, we compare the boundary Gram operator of one wing with the product of its marginals on the cut side and the remaining three sides. A reference system with at most eight unsaturated sites then controls a physical cut of arbitrary length. Recursion over overlapping rectangles gives the gap. We also obtain a gap on all simple tori, including those of fixed circumference. In free squares, boundary effects on fixed local observables decay exponentially with the buffer width. By the stability theorems of Nachtergaele, Sims and Young, weak quasi-local perturbations with stretched-exponentially decaying interaction terms preserve the bulk GNS gap and the finite-torus gap at bounded aspect ratio.

papers.title: Vertex operator algebras from Flohr's second family realising doubles of near-group categories $\mathbb{Z}_n+n$ for even $n$
papers.abstract: We study Flohr's second family $\mathcal{W}(2,3k)$, with generating weights $2$ and $3k$ and central charge $1-24k$ for $k\in\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. We realise these algebras and their subalgebras $\mathcal{W}(2,8k)$, generated in weights $2$ and $8k$, by deforming the conformal vector of the vertex algebra of the rank-one lattice $L=\mathbb{Z}\beta$, $(\beta,\beta)=2k$. We prove strong rationality and compute the simple modules and modular data for $\mathcal{W}(2,8k)$ at all $k$ and $\mathcal{W}(2,3k)$ at integral $k$. For nonintegral $k$ we describe the Neveu–Schwarz sector of the $\mathcal{W}(2,3k)$ superalgebra. The same conformal vector makes the lattice vertex algebra of the index-two sublattice $2L$ an extension of $\mathcal{W}(2,8k)$. Its modules in the representation category of $\mathcal{W}(2,8k)$ form a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded category with neutral component of near-group type $\mathbb{Z}_{4k}+4k$. We realise the Drinfeld centres of the graded category and its neutral component by regular vertex operator algebras, using the orthogonal complement of a primitive norm-$8k$ vector in the $E_8$ lattice and conformal shifts to match the ribbon structures. For integral $k$ we give a Leavitt algebra realisation of the near-group category and derive finite quantum dilogarithm identities. We also realise the centres of its quotients by central lifts of the order-$2s$ subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_{4k}$ for $s^2\mid k$, including twisted Haagerup–Izumi-type centres over $\mathbb{Z}_{2s}$ when $k=s^2$. We classify the Galois conjugates of the centre modular data with positive categorical dimensions, determine the Witt classes of the $\mathcal{W}(2,3k)$ representation categories for integral $k$, and describe the near-group module categories and their Morita duals.

papers.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
papers.abstract: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.
